side_a: CC 4.2.1 Humanity-accord authority signs nothing outside this enumeration.
side_b: CC 3.4.1 The accord-holder verdict on an agent's human-dignity conduct, carried as `accord:human_dignity:v1` (`attested_key_id` = the agent scored)
note: The enumeration of CC 4.2.1 holds neither accord:human_dignity nor the accord heartbeat accord:lifecycle ("accord-holder self-attestation about the accord", CC 3.4.1); both are registered leaves only an accord_holder may emit, and transitions.json admits each on one holder's act. A verifier built from 4.2.1 refuses them as out of role; one built from the registry admits them. C051 records the same gap for the roster-change objects of CC 4.2.6.

side_a: CC 4.2.3 name the three holders' hybrid keys (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65), one per person
side_b: CC 4.5.1 a holder's primary and backup keys are one holder, under whichever of their keys is live
note: CC 4.2.3 seats one key per holder; CC 4.5.1 counts a holder under a primary or a backup key. No section says how a backup key is seated, pinned in the bundle or recognised by a verifier, and CC 4.2.6 gives recovery by a pre-committed rotation, never a standing second key. A halt or a sign-off signed by a backup key is honoured under 4.5.1 and refused under 4.2.3.

side_a: CC 1.16.5: Appointment, rotation, recusal, and appeals are external to this system’s control and follow explicit anti-capture rules.
side_b: CC 4.3: A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else;
note: Who answers an agent's deferral: Wise Authorities appointed under the Annex B charter, outside the system (CC 1.16.5, CC 1.9 'designated'), or whoever the agent's steward seated by a delegates_to, and the steward itself where no seat row exists (CC 4.3). CC 4.3 says 'the charter governs the designated body' and does not say how that body relates to a conferred seat. The CC 4.5.1 register also records 'none' as the exit from the WA relation, while CC 4.3 lets the conferrer end a seat by withdraws. CC 4.3 is the normative, wire-checked rule.

side_a: CC 5.2 "all current identity_occurrences of C.attesting_key_id"
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3 "is not counted toward the target, is not a deficit, receives no keys for the cohort and pulls nothing for it"
note: CC 5.2's enforcement block has the substrate MUST wrap the content key to every current occurrence at self and every member at family; CC 6.1.5.3 gives a node its owner denied (and a server-class node by default) no key. The 5.2 prose paragraph 'Which of a member's nodes' sides with 6.1.5.3; the pseudo-code and the 'Composition with the at-rest encryption flow' paragraph do not carry the allow list.

side_a: CC 5.2 "the listing, the holding claims and, by asking a member's node, the content; never the roster"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.1 "opt OUT of the mandatory DEK cascade and are Commons-tier (plaintext, holding claims at federation scope, no DEK)"
note: CC 5.2's table gives a public room's rows the audience 'the claimed nodes of the roster's members', and a node holds a row only when in its audience; CC 4.4.3.2.1 and 5.4.2 call the room Commons-tier, whose audience in the same table is every node. Whether a non-member node may hold and re-serve a public room's content differs. Beside C254 (discoverability), which is not this.

side_a: CC 6.1.5 "(governed by LRU-only): no holding claim, no compress request, no rarest-first biasing"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "hides who published a federation-scope item from the nodes that store it, from the directory, and, with shaping, from an observer of the network"
note: 'Anonymous tier' names two things. In CC 6.1.5 (SR-2), 6.1.5.3, 6.1 (WW-2) and 6.1.8 (RB-1) it is a class of content with no holding claim, outside the witness and exempt from anti-entropy; in CC 5.4.6 it is an onion transport for federation-scope items that are stored and listed in the directory. Whether an item published through the tier carries holding claims and is replicated differs by which section is read.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "key records and identity occurrences, which are public and are what let the two peers seal to each other"
note: The dependency closure withholds an occurrence whose attester's owner-binding is not announced at federation scope; the forwarder's 'serves openly' list and the stranger-carried set ('key records and revocations, occurrences') name occurrences with no such condition. An unannounced node's occurrence is served to a stranger under one reading and withheld under the other. The 'never listed' MUST of the same section supports the closure.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2 "the bootstrap kinds, the allegiance facts and the pairing plane are all a not-yet-Rooted sealed link carries"
side_b: CC 5.3.4 "and every row a bounded cohort delivers to that peer as its member under"
note: CC 5.3.4 lists four things that cross before Rooted (adding rows addressed to the peer and every bounded-cohort row delivered to it as a member); CC 3.3.6.2 says three are all the link carries. A reader of 3.3.6.2 alone holds family and community rows back from a member's not-yet-Rooted node. CC 5.3.4 is the home and the fuller list.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: A producer MUST NOT ship a dimension family this Part does not register.
side_b: CC 3.1.7: The ProducerSteward fallback remains only for the open-vocabulary space this Part deliberately leaves open.
note: One sentence forbids shipping any unregistered family and a neighbour orders a substrate to fail emission on a family with no registry row (namespace_family_unregistered); two others keep an admissible open vocabulary and the x_private range. A reader of the first refuses a party's own unregistered dimension, a reader of the second admits it under the producer-steward fallback. The closing paragraph of CC 3.1.7 (open vocabulary is for a party's own dimensions, never a shipped component's) supports the second, with the MUST NOT bound to shipped components.

side_a: CC 6.1.5 "Durability is a **per-item choice the owner makes on publish**."
side_b: CC 6.1.5.2 "Consent *authorizes*, the owner *elects* — a pin requires **both**."
note: 'Owner' and 'durable' name two things. In CC 6.1.5 and 6.1.5.1 the item's publisher marks it durable and the swarm replicates it to the target across the cohort's live nodes; in CC 6.1.5.2 content is durable on a node only if that node's owner lists its class in `pinned_class`, and is otherwise cache that descends first. CC 6.1.5.3 runs both at every tier without saying which governs when a member's node has not elected the class: whether that node counts as a holder and keeps the item differs.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.4 The perceptual-hash tripwire likewise fires at every scope-widening promotion
side_b: CC 4.5.7 Detection runs **only at the publish/share seam of enabled groups**
note: CC 1.13.3.4 and 3.1.3.4 make the tripwire unconditional at every widening; CC 4.5.7 makes the matcher an opt-in the group's moderate-holder enables per group, on a hash list the operator provisions, and CC 4.5.13 repeats "only at enabled groups' publish/share seam". A promotion into a group that has not enabled a list is hash-matched under the first and not under the second. Neither says whether the CSAM list is the always-on case.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.4 **substrate-protective perceptual-hash tripwire at every scope-*widening* promotion event**, never on the device, never inside a private cohort
side_b: CC 3.2 runs on the post exactly as it runs on a promotion into the Commons — never inside a private cohort, never on the device
note: A widening from self to family, or from family to a gated community, is a scope-widening promotion that lands inside a private cohort. "Every widening" (CC 3.1.3.4: "Every widening is an act on specific bytes ... each with its own emission and tripwire") matches it; "never inside a private cohort" and the next sentence of 1.13.3.4 (only a promotion into the Commons or a post into a public room is matched) do not. The Commons-or-public-room reading is the one the privacy position supports.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.2: `delegates_to(parent_key → student_canonical_hash, scope: [consent_revocation])` for minors
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: emits `delegates_to(canonical_hash → agent_key, scope: [consent_revocation])` when the proxy is set up.
note: Direction of the proxy edge. Rule 3 (CC 2.4.1.1, CC 2.3.2.2) runs from the subject's canonical hash to the key that will revoke for it; the FERPA row runs from the parent's key to the student's hash, which under rule 3 gives the parent no path to withdraw for the student. CC 2.4.1.1 is the home; the table row is reversed.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: execute as the same tombstone row — plane, target digest, the authorising `takedown_notice`'s id; never content
side_b: CC 7.5.5: a person's deletion inside the sealed record is the same tombstone by digest on the record's plane, citing the subject's own withdrawal or the order, written by whoever holds custody.
note: The one tombstone row carries an authorising takedown_notice id and CC 2.4.1.1's door refuses a tombstone without the notice (purge_unauthorised); CC 7.5.5 (and CC 4.5.3's own erasure paragraph: 'the ordinary tombstone by digest per plane') has a tombstone authorised by a subject's withdrawal with no notice. One implementer refuses the erasure tombstone, the other writes it.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: A duty-holder's notice is admitted by the [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5) enforced-admission rule and reaches the bytes plane only.
side_b: CC 7.5.5: a lawful order to destroy sealed material is a `takedown_notice:court_order:v1` executed as the tombstone by digest of [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) with every purge guarantee
note: A court_order notice is a duty-holder basis (immediate-removal, bytes plane only, destroyed on receipt); CC 7.5.5 has it destroy a sealed retirement record (identity record, audit trail, logs: rows on other planes) with 'every purge guarantee', which in CC 4.5.3 belongs to the root-cosigned steward_purge (any plane, 72 h dwell, whole or not at all). Which reach and which dwell a court order has differs by section.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: `CourtOrder` — the operator follows the court's stated timeline.
side_b: CC 4.5.3: An immediate-removal basis has no window: its bytes are destroyed on receipt (item 2).
note: CourtOrder is in the immediate-removal list, so a reachable holder destroys on receipt; the per-basis dispatch gives the same basis the court's own timeline. An order that allows 30 days is destroyed at once under one sentence and on the court's date under the other. The Annex transition (destroy_bytes on admitted) supports destroy on receipt.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.2: if now > deadline and completion is None:
side_b: CC 3.3.1: Breach is therefore: the window passed **and** the row is still present with none of the three composers against it.
note: The watcher of CC 4.4.3.5.2 raises the breach when the producer has emitted no consent:deletion_complete, so the emission alone clears it; CC 3.3.1 D1 says the emission never substitutes and the test is the row's presence. A producer that emits deletion_complete and keeps the row breaches under one and not the other. CC 3.3.1 also says the watcher is cancelled only by withdraws, supersedes or hard deletion; D1 is marked normative.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.2: if now > deadline and completion is None:
side_b: manifests/reactions.json consent:deletion_sla:{days}: the breach reaction at the close of the sla clock is emitted unless the target was withdrawn, superseded or purged; consent:deletion_complete is not among the conditions
note: The data follows CC 3.3.1 D1 (the row's absence), not the CC 4.4.3.5.2 watcher (the producer's deletion_complete). The same data row starts the clock on 'withdrawn of target' and excuses the breach on 'withdrawn of target', so as written a subject's withdrawal both starts and clears the watch; the text's D1 means the producer's own composer.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: `CourtOrder` — the operator follows the court's stated timeline.
side_b: manifests/reactions.json takedown_notice:{basis}, leaves NcmecCsam, PerceptualHashCsam, TvecTerrorist, GifctCip, CourtOrder: on admitted, stop_serving and destroy_bytes, force must
note: The data destroys a CourtOrder target at admission with the other immediate bases; the per-basis dispatch gives it the court's timeline. Data agrees with the 'no window, destroyed on receipt' sentence of the same section.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: authorised by a cosigned `takedown_notice` under the trust root's `consensus_protocol` with basis `steward_purge`
side_b: manifests/transitions.json takedown_notice:{basis}: one attest transition for every basis, role takedown, policy selfAct (one voice); no cosigned policy for the steward_purge leaf and no steward_purge row in governance_policy.tsv
note: The text makes a steward_purge notice a row cosigned by the trust root's seats under its protocol; the transition data admits every takedown_notice basis on one signature by a takedown duty-holder. A kernel executing the data admits a one-signer purge notice that the text's door refuses.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: `temporary` (14d auto-expire, default)
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.6: `consent:state:granted` + envelope `valid_until = asserted_at + 14d` + auto-renew dimension on interaction (consumer-policy concern)
note: A temporary grant lapses 14 days after it was granted under CC 3.3.1 and 14 days after the last interaction under CC 4.4.3.5.6, which adds an auto-renew the first does not state; who signs the renewal is not said, and a grant row is the subject's to sign (CC 3.3.1 Emitted by). CC 3.4.13 and CC 3.4.12 forbid auto-renew for their own grants.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "Expiry is judged on the instants the parties signed, never on a receiver's clock."
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "Every window of this table is measured by each node from the instant it first held the proposal, never from a signed instant of the proposer or of a cosigner."
note: Opposite clocks for a membership change. CC 3.1.3.2 concludes that every node gives the same verdict for the same rows; CC 4.5.13 (whose table has the invite and removal windows) concludes that two nodes may close a window at different moments, and adds that the first-held instant is what every window in this document runs from. That last sentence also contradicts CC 2.6.7 (W runs from the signed asserted_at) and CC 3.2 T4a (the attach window runs from a cosignature's signed_at). If the proposal's signed expiry and the policy window are two things, neither section says so.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 The latch is idempotent, so a replayed or second row changes nothing.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.3 A resumption authorizes ending a *single named* `constitutional` halt, not resumption-in-general.
note: Two holders fire two halts (two ids) for one emergency. Under 4.2.1.1 the second row changes nothing: one latch, the first id, the first fuse. Under 4.2.1.3 and the confirmation rule ("names the halt by id") each halt is its own object. If the majority confirms the second id, a single-latch node sees a confirmation of a halt it never latched and lapses at the first fuse; a per-halt node stays paused. Likewise a resumption of the first id frees a single-latch node and leaves a per-halt node paused under the second. Neither section says which halt is "the currently-active" one when two have arrived.

side_a: CC 5.2: or each `member.key_id` in the named family's roster (family).
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: At every sealed write the substrate wraps the content's DEK to every current recipient occurrence and emits one `key_grant` row per wrap.
note: CC 5.2 wraps a family write once per member key and names the wrap target by key id; CC 4.4.3.4.1 (the cascade's home) wraps to every occurrence of every recipient, and CC 5.2's own next paragraph says the target is the occurrence's encryption_pubkeys, never a signing key. Under the first a family member's second device reads nothing. The home supports per occurrence.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: `hard_case:legal_hold_set` / `:lifted` / `:violation_attempt` make set, lift, and any deletion-during-hold observable (spoliation is liability).
side_b: CC 4.5.3: The exception is an immediate-removal `legal_basis` below, where a reachable holder MUST destroy the bytes on receipt of the notice.
note: Neither section says which wins when a takedown or a steward_purge reaches a record under a legal_hold. CC 4.4.3.2.8 names only the retention schedule and consent-driven descent as overridden and treats any deletion during a hold as a violation attempt; CC 4.5.3 and CC 6.1.2.2 make destruction on receipt total. One implementer destroys held evidence, the other keeps prohibited bytes.

side_a: CC 7.3.3 "any system assessed at **RM ≥ 4** opens the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation. That is the one trigger"
side_b: CC 8.8.3 "A system must pass a CRE before deployment if it meets any of:"
note: CC 7.3.3 (three times) makes RM ≥ 4 the one trigger of the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation and Annex D only the criteria it applies; Annex D-1 is headed 'Trigger criteria' and requires the evaluation on compute above 10^26 FLOP, transactional authority above $10M a day, or a recursive event, with no mention of RM. A low-RM system that meets D-1, or an RM 4 system that meets none of it, is evaluated under one and not the other.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "`authority_id` names a key: a `federation_keys.key_id`, or an organisation"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8 "Its own walk from its own edges reaches the issuing authority for the row's class, and that authority's charter declares the class."
note: CC 2.4.1.2.1 and CC 4.4.3.4.3 let anyone be a licence authority under a bare key; CC 4.4.3.8 honours a licence only where the authority's charter declares the class, and CC 4.4.3.2.8 carries that declaration on a signed community record. A bare key has no charter, so its licences are honoured by no reader under 4.4.3.8 and folded as licensure under 2.4.1.2.1. The CC 4.3 seat rule ('holds a live licence from that authority') does not say which reading it takes.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2 "pull-only `ContentFetch` (CC 5.3.3.5 E2), as for broadcast; no selective-forwarding relay role"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.4 "a relay forwards only the layers downstream asked for"
note: CC 5.3.3.2 gives every realtime profile no relay tree (direct links at small N, pull-only at large N), CC 2.1 says push goes 'never through a relay tree', CC 6.1.6 says the realtime profile 'has no relay role' and CC 5.3.3.2.1 that 'no relay reads' the layer header. CC 5.3.3.4 has a call's layers taken from parents of the member relay tree with relays forwarding by layer, and CC 5.4.6 has 'the tree's relays' verify each chunk. Whether a call's chunks pass through member relays differs.

side_a: CC 3.4.13: So a person with no assurance on record uses their own and their family's scopes freely
side_b: CC 3.2: **No minor `user` identity operates without a live adult steward.**
note: A person with no age assurance reads as under 13 (the fail-secure rule), hence a minor. CC 3.2 and CC 3.4.13 Q4 ('A guardian-less minor goes dark for general operation') stop a minor with no guardian from operating; the fail-secure paragraph lets the same person use self and family scope freely with no guardian. One build blocks every unassured new user, the other does not. The fail-secure paragraph is the newer ruling (C001) and reads the guardian rule as binding an attested minor.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding, and admission MUST refuse the promotion.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: **Announcing starts on,** its cost on screen.
note: With no assurance on record an owner resolves to under_13, which implies minor (CC 3.4.13), so admission refuses the federation-scope binding for every person who has not yet shown a provider-rung signal; CC 4.5.13 has announcing on by default 'for nearly everyone'. Whether 'resolves to the minor band' means attested as a minor, or includes the fail-secure default, is unstated and decides who is reachable.

side_a: CC 3.4.13: fail-secure MUST mean the report reaches a standing Wise-Authority / mandated-report endpoint via WBD even with no guardian present
side_b: CC 4.3: there is no roster of permitted Wise Authorities and a substrate checks none.
note: The help floor requires a standing Wise Authority that receives a child's report with no guardian present. CC 4.3 seats a Wise Authority only by the deferring party's own row, or for a ward by whoever holds the binding, and keeps no standing body on the wire. For a child whose guardian is the threat, no rule says who the standing receiver is or who seated it.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: "A substrate observing emission on a family with no registry row (provisional or ratified) MUST surface it as a conformance failure (`namespace_family_unregistered`), never admit-and-wait."
side_b: CC 3.1.7: "An unregistered family has no owning component, no polarity and no reserved rule, so a consumer resolving its authority falls through to the producer-steward default."
note: What a node does with a row on a family that has no registry row. R2 says it never admits under a defaulted authority; R1 says its authority resolves to the producer-steward default, and "Where the fallback remains" keeps that default for an open-vocabulary space it does not define (an unrowed family, or the open leaves of a registered one). R1 also calls an ungated family described only in CC 3.3 conformant though unregistered. The row is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. The closed-stem passages support refusal.

side_a: CC 2.4 "A `dimension` on **any** of the five MUST resolve through the namespace exactly as it does on `scores`"
side_b: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
note: The same finding as under row_shape, seen from the gate: CC 2.4 has the admitting substrate resolve every dimension; CC 2.1's member table says the substrate does not parse it.

side_a: CC 3.4.7.3: "A `federation_keys` key whose `identity_type` set contains `node` MUST NOT also contain `agent` or `user`."
side_b: CC 4.5.8.4: "Forbid any cohabitation at the wire layer (substrate enforces gates by membership; constitutional/substrate cohabitation discipline is consumer/operator policy per CC 4.5.8.1)"
note: CC 4.5.8.4 lists, under what the role-set rule does not do, forbidding any cohabitation, and leaves the discipline to operator policy. CC 3.4.7.1 and CC 3.4.7.3 Clause A forbid one pair with MUST NOT. A key record carrying node with agent is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. Clause A is the later and specific rule, and CC 3.2 leans on it.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7: "the fingerprint the first ten lowercase base32 characters of sha256(ed25519 public key)"
side_b: CC 2.6.8: "SHOULD raise the fingerprint length (16 characters, 80 bits, moves the bound to 2⁴⁰)"
note: The format is stated as ten characters, normative, in CC 2.6.8 and in the signed-object table; the same paragraph of CC 2.6.8 tells a large deployment to use sixteen. A verifier that recomputes ten characters refuses a sixteen-character id. Nothing says how a reader learns which length a label uses.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: Every reserved-prefix role — `trusted_publisher` reserving `content_rating:*`
side_b: data: manifests/namespace_registry.json: content_rating:{scheme}:{rating} has reserved false and no reserved_rule
note: CC 4.4.3.8 and CC 3.2 treat content_rating:* as a reserved prefix whose emitter role is conferred by delegation, and CC 3.4.7 has a substrate reject a reserved-prefix row from any other key. The registry, which CC 3.1.7 makes the enforcement surface, carries the family unreserved, so a matcher built from it admits a rating from any key. The CC 3.1.9.2 catalogue row speaks of 'the trusted-publisher emitter rule' and CC 3.4 lists no such reservation.

side_a: CC 3.4.7.1: A key satisfies a reserved-prefix gate iff the required role is one of its held roles.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: leaving a reserved-prefix role with **no** named plane leaves it self-assertable, which is the hole this rule closes.
note: One test is set membership in the key's identity_type, which CC 3.4.5 calls self-asserted; the other requires a live delegates_to from a root the asking node trusts, resolved at use. The registry's detector rule reads 'identity_type contains lenscore_detector'. A substrate built from CC 3.4.7.1 alone admits a detection:* row from any key that lists the role. CC 3.2 and CC 4.4.3.8 support the delegation test.

side_a: CC 3.2 "a strict majority of the live roster, the proposer included, or the lone path after its window with no objection"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3 "elapses and no strict majority of the *other* members objects"
note: CC 3.2 and CC 4.5.12.2 let the lone path land only with no objection; CC 3.3.6.3 lets it land unless a strict majority of the other keys object. With three keys and one objecting, a new key is admitted (or a key evicted) under 3.3.6.3 and not under 3.2. The policy rows self_roster_add and self_roster_evict (cancel: 'more than 1/2 of the others') support CC 3.3.6.3.

side_a: CC 2.1 "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
side_b: CC 3.1.3 "`attested_key_id` is the recipient occurrence"
note: CC 2.1 has every scores row at family, community or affiliations name its own producer in attested_key_id and refuses a third party; a key grant is a scores row placed at the content's scope whose attested_key_id is the recipient and whose signer is the sealer (CC 3.1.3, 3.3.2), and group:roster names the group there. CC 2.1 states no exception; the family model records one.

side_a: CC 2.1 "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "the content's scope (attested = recipient, AV-84 exception)"
note: The family model's placement cell for key_grant:{axis} records an exception to the producer rule that CC 2.1 does not state. The data and CC 3.1.3 agree; CC 2.1 is the side that lacks the exception.

side_a: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "resolved through manifests/namespace_registry.json on all five row types"
note: CC 2.1 leaves the dimension unparsed by the substrate; CC 2.6.1.7, CC 2.4 (the dimension gate) and CC 3.1.7 (namespace_family_unregistered, score_outside_declared_polarity) have the admitting substrate resolve it against the registry and refuse. A row on an unregistered family is admitted under one and refused under the other. The rest of the document supports the gate.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "their **agent** (the agent's local key) are two occurrences of one user identity that share one **Self DEK**"
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "An agent signs no item of a person's queue: the person's choices are the person's."
note: CC 3.3.6.3 defines the roster as the identity_occurrence rows under the fedID and lets "any live roster key" sign as the fedID for every owner act (consent, owner-binding, root acceptance, approving a device), and CC 4.5.13 counts a vote signed by any key of the fedID. If the agent's key is an occurrence of the user, it signs all of these. CC 4.5.13, CC 4.3 and CC 3.3.6.3 ("an agent's occurrence is single-signer") deny it. The denial is the later text and the one CC 1.13.2 supports.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
side_b: CC 3.1.3: "`attested_key_id` is the recipient occurrence; the envelope carries the key's identity on that axis and the wrap"
note: A key grant is a scores row placed at the content's scope, signed by the sealer, with the recipient in attested_key_id: a third party there. CC 2.1 states one exception to the producer rule (delegates_to) and the next paragraph puts a key grant's recipient among subject_key_ids. Read from CC 2.1 alone a community key grant is refused. family_model.json records the grant as an exception ("attested = recipient occurrence"), which supports CC 3.1.3.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A row naming a key outside its audience is refused `subject_outside_audience`."
side_b: data family_default_row.json: "in_audience": "no"
note: The default subject_rule of every family (157 of 184 cells, source code-v61) reads in_audience "no" and the default replication audience is cohort_plus_subjects: the shipped store admits a targeted row naming an outsider and serves it to them. The text (CC 2.1, CC 5.2) refuses the row. No departure reason or conflict row records the difference.

side_a: CC 2.4.1 "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: CC 3.2 "a new guardian's `delegates_to` carried as a `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) replaces the prior binding"
note: CC 2.4.1 confines supersedes to the prior row's own attester, and CC 3.5.1 rule 4 evaluates another attester's composer as a separate chain; CC 3.2 has a new guardian, a different signer, supersede the old guardian's binding. Whether a guardian can be displaced by the incoming guardian's row alone differs. CC 3.2 also writes one row as two types (a delegates_to 'carried as' a supersedes) against the closed type slot of CC 2.4.

side_a: CC 2.4.1 "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json "verb": "supersede"
note: In the transitions data the supersede verb of group:roster and membership:{stage} is signed by role `member` (source code-v61), not `author`: another member's row replaces the standing one. CC 2.4.1 states no such case. CC 3.1.3 (a roster version 'cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`') supports the data.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 "it does not un-say the prior record, it ends its liveness"
side_b: CC 3.5.1 "carries the prior's `asserted_at` and is a placement, never a competing successor"
note: A supersedes ends the prior row's liveness (CC 2.4.1 'replaces', CC 3.4.5.1); a widening is a supersedes (CC 4.4.3.3.1) yet is a placement that leaves the narrower row standing (CC 3.5.1, CC 5.2 boundary case, CC 3.2). A reader of CC 4.4.3.3.1 alone retires the narrower row on widening; whether the owner's self copy stays live and whether un-widening is possible differ. C132 and C133 are two instances of this at the owner-binding.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.5: "There is no relay tree; the small-group realtime profile of [CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2) pushes on direct links"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.4: "A member MAY take each layer of a stream from a different parent of the member relay tree"
note: E2, E1 sentence 1, the CC 5.3.3.2 profile table and CC 2.1 deny any media relay role in realtime delivery; CC 5.3.3.4, 5.3.3.2.3 (member relay verifies and forwards chunks) and 5.4.6 (the tree's relays) build one. One implementer ships direct links only, the other a forwarding tree. The later-written sections (binding, trailer, layered multipath) support the tree.

side_a: CC 2.1: "on direct links and never through a relay tree"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3: "A member relay forwards a binding it has verified to every other leg, and only when the binding's publisher is the peer it heard it from"
note: Same rule as the row above, read from the grammar side: CC 2.1 says push never crosses a relay tree; the chunk format defines what a member relay forwards and when. Push through a member relay is either forbidden or specified.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "Chat and files ride a shaped link only when one end of it is shaped-only."
side_b: CC 5.4.3: "A shaped link carries rows: statements, posts, messages, reactions, the small images that fit the budget, and the control traffic of the planes."
note: Between two offering nodes that hold a shaped link, one paragraph sends chat over the unshaped link beside it and the other (with item 4, "ordinary rows are shaped") puts messages on the shaped link. Whether a message between two servers is covered differs. The carriage paragraph is the more specific.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "a scoped body MAY ride the members' **identity-plane link** on three terms"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "crosses a forwarder only one that has said yes, a consented contact or, as last resort, a serve seat; a stranger is offered none"
note: The first paragraph lets a room body cross any non-member transport node between two members on three terms, none of them the node's consent; "Who carries what" adds that the forwarder must be a carrier that said yes. Two phones behind NATs with only a stranger between them exchange a room body under one reading and not the other. The later paragraph and CC 5.4.3 support the consent condition.

side_a: CC 3.2: "A portable root minted by any trio enters via delegation. The shipped default enters via ceremony."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "It is minted by the [CC 4.2.1](#4.2.1) conferral ceremony and owes nothing to any prior root."
note: Who mints a portable root and on which plane: CC 3.2 T2 says any trio, entering by delegation; CC 4.4.3.8 and CC 4.2.1 say the conferral ceremony, a co-scrub by a strict majority of the standing accord roster. CC 3.2 T2 itself says root identity is conferred by ceremony, so the rest of the text supports side B.

side_a: CC 3.2: "Consumers pin `community_key_id: ciris-canonical` and resolve the live member set via `resolve_community`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "That names the founders of `ciris-canonical`, who are the three accord holders `A1`, `B1`, `C1`"
note: Whose signatures the shipped default pin trusts: CC 3.2 (and CC 5.3.4) resolve the live member set, which by CC 3.2 includes serve nodes seated as role member; CC 4.4.3.8 says the pin names the founders and never a serving install's key. The same paragraph also writes the pin as a policy value where CC 4.4.3.8 says the set is the reader's own acceptance edges and nothing else. CC 3.2 "Infrastructure does not vote" supports the founders reading.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard).
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame
note: The outer nonce is SHA-256(label, link_id, link_seq) with no stream id in it. One counter per link gives distinct nonces across the streams of a link; one counter per (link, stream), each starting at 0, gives two streams on one link the same outer nonce, and a receiver built the other way cannot open. The nonce formula supports per link; the loss-recovery paragraph is written per (link, stream).

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`
note: One sentence lays out the v1 trailer (64 bytes, domain av-chunk-sig:v1) and says the shipping form is another (72 bytes, domain v2, budget eight bytes lower) without laying it out. The relay rule still reads "take the last 64 bytes as the trailer". An implementer of the written layout and one of the shipping form refuse each other's chunks as av_chunk_trailer_invalid. CC 2.6.1.8 only says the trailer stays a raw signature.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 are the only shapes this Part registers
side_b: CC 3.4.11 provider/government rungs MAY further qualify `{level}` with a `{verifier_key}` / `{credential_class}`
note: Same sentence. The registry and the match vectors carry only age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version}; age_assurance: is a reserved stem, so CC 3.1.7 refuses an unclaimed leaf under it as namespace_family_unregistered. A producer using the MAY emits a row every conformant substrate refuses. The registry supports "only two shapes".

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds"
side_b: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
note: The home table gives rule 2 one condition (the kept list) and says a node MUST admit when a line holds. CC 3.2 adds a second condition for one family. Built from CC 2.4.1.1 alone, a node admits a compromised node key's withdrawal of its own owner. CC 3.2 is the specific rule; the home neither states nor cites the gate.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "Its later `withdraws` against any row carrying that hash in `subject_key_ids` is admitted under rule 3."
side_b: CC 3.3.14: "The proxy attaches only after that out-of-band establishment, reaches no row on the kept list of CC 2.4.1.1, and is suspended while two bindings for the same person compete."
note: CC 2.4.1.1 lets the data-holding agent set the proxy up by its own delegates_to and admits its later withdrawal with no further test. CC 3.3.14 adds two conditions: identity established out of band first, and suspension while bindings compete. A withdrawal is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. Beside C276, which covers the binding and not the proxy's conditions.

side_a: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
side_b: manifests/transitions.json (ownership:{relation}:{target_kind}:{version}, withdraw): "when(verb=withdraw,has=wa_adjudication_ref) one wa_adjudication:{state}@admitted[id=ref:wa_adjudication_ref] else refuse"
note: The data puts the recovery guard on the ownership:* mirror row and fires it only when the reference is present; the owner-binding itself (self:delegates_to) has one transition, authorize, and no withdraw, supersede or lapse. The text's gate (a subject or delegate withdrawal with no reference is refused) and the owner's own withdrawal are not in the data.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: No single signer admits an amendment, and no single signer vetoes one by refusing to sign.
side_b: CC 4.5.1: amendment authority rests with the founder as steward, and any accord-holder may propose an amendment
note: Read apart, one sentence denies any single decider and the other names one until the scale gate. The paragraph order shows the first is the step 5 sign-off after the gate; the sentence itself carries no such condition.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster.
side_b: CC 4.5.1.2: before the scale gate it is exercised by the steward under the scale gate in [CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1).
note: Before the gate, CC 4.5.1 keeps a quorum of at least a strict majority; CC 4.5.1.2 has the steward exercise the entrenched ratification. constitution/constants.tsv entrenchment_quorum says 'never lower, before or after the scale gate', which sides with a counted majority before the gate and against the steward alone.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "Each node's setup chooses whether that node **announces**, which in this section means one thing"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "Every node announces its identity destination, so an observer sees that each member node exists and is reachable."
note: Announce is fixed to one meaning (the owner-binding at federation scope) and then used for the Reticulum announce "which every routing node emits". For a node in anonymous mode ("The node announces nothing") the second sense decides whether its transport destination is broadcast at all; the two readings give an observable and an unobservable node.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "(1) The owner's per-node policy is held at the owner's `self` scope."
side_b: CC 3.3.7 "It carries `cohort_scope: federation` (the grant itself is a public governance record)."
note: CC 6.1.5.3 makes the allow list the `cohorts` member of the owner's consent:replication grant and says the policy is held at self and never names one cohort to another; CC 3.3.7 places that grant at federation scope as a public record. A public grant with a `cohorts` member publishes the owner's cohort list.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.1 "`family_id` / `community_id` ride the envelope"
side_b: CC 2.1 "So `family_id` is consulted in-substrate and never on the wire to non-members."
note: CC 1.13.3.1 concedes that an observer learns a group exists, its rough size and churn from ids on the envelope and hard_case events in the log; CC 2.1 and the CC 5.2 table ('nothing of the content, of the roster or of who holds it') say a non-member sees none of it. Parts 2 and 5 agree with each other.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.2.1: A `quorum:2/3` collective that grows to 5 members still admits at **2** signatures
note: Absolute M of 2 in a roster of 5 against the CC 4.5.13 corridor in which enact is never below a strict majority of the base (side B as recorded in C284; not re-quoted here). Still in the text; whether the declared protocol or the policy row decides a cosigned admission is the open question of C283.

side_a: CC 3.2: a minor has at most one live guardian, transferred by `supersedes`, never accreted
side_b: CC 3.4.13: M-of-N co-guardianship is supported as a verified DAG over `delegates_to`
note: One guardian per minor, superseded and never accreted, against a set of N guardians with a quorum M. Still in the text on both sides; CC 3.4.13 Q7's seven rules and the CC 3.2 guardianship clause it cites support the set.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "The substrate MUST refuse such a row whose `asserted_at` precedes the receiver's clock by more than `W`"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: "A row signed by a key that is still live admits at any age"
note: Whether W binds every chain-judged row or only a row whose signer has lost standing at receipt. A new device syncing old consent rows or licences admits them on one reading and refuses them asserted_at_stale on the other. Open in the conflict table.

side_a: CC 3.2 the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`)
side_b: CC 4.2.1 The signer-chosen `asserted_at` plays no part, as for the fuse
note: Ruled 2026-11-11 for the node's latch instant; CC 3.2's list of what a verdict reads still judges the edge at asserted_at. A node that cut its edge after a pre-signed row's asserted_at and before the row arrived is reached under 3.2 and not under 4.2.1.

side_a: CC 4.2.6 within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 admitted at a node before that node's own fuse lapses
note: One table measures the confirmation window from "the halt", the other from each node's receipt on its own clock. A node that received the halt late admits a confirmation another node, measuring from the first publication, would treat as too late. CC 4.2.1.1 and the window-clock rule of CC 4.5.13 support per-node receipt.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 The nonce is single-use within `valid_until`.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 So a sealed row signed months earlier is live when published
note: The signed bytes carry valid_until and the duplicate rule is bounded by it, but no sentence says whether a halt published after its own valid_until fires. A pre-signed row kept sealed for months either needs a far-future valid_until or is dead on publication; one implementer checks it, another follows "asserted_at plays no part" and ignores both instants.

side_a: CC 5.1: | Member addition | Epoch advances — an MLS Add is a commit, so the exporter secret and every per-stream DEK derived from it change;
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: Removal rotates the epoch; admission does not.

A reader who takes them as one either rotates the content key on every join or lets a joiner read the whole current content epoch. The rest of the text supports two keys.

side_a: CC 3.2: a minor has at most one live guardian, transferred by `supersedes`, never accreted
side_b: CC 3.4.13: M-of-N co-guardianship is supported as a verified DAG over `delegates_to`
note: One guardian per minor against a set of co-guardians acting M of N (Q7). Still in the text at CC 3.2; held for the steward.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: "**The floor in a small room** is the smaller of two voices and the roster's size, so a room of one elects itself by its own ballot"
side_b: data governance_policy.tsv: a locked room elects its moderator: ballot = the roster in worthiness order, one ballot per person
note: The moderator_election row carries floor "2 voices" (governance_policy.json floor_rule kind voices, count 2; min_count community 2) with no smaller-of clause. A kernel that executes the row leaves a room of one locked; the text and constants.tsv community_floor_voices say min(2, roster size).

side_b: CC 3.4.7.3: "The `identity_occurrence` half yields **at most one** anchor, and the custody half yields **at most one**"
note: Whether an identity_occurrence makes its identity a steward for Clause D. The definition and CC 3.2 (the folds never read occurrences) say no; the Cardinality paragraph counts an occurrence anchor. An agent would be admitted to act through a node on one reading and refused on the other.

note: Two wire shapes for one act, and two effects: CC 2.3.2.2 says the admitted binding lets the bound key withdraw under rule 2; CC 3.3.14 says it is a claim readers weigh that admits nothing. CC 3.3.14 is the later, normative entry and the registry row follows it.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "Admission to a `family` or `community` is two consents, never one"
side_b: CC 4.5.13 "Where admission is open — `open:self_admit`, anyone signs their own admission — no single vote excludes"
note: Still there: CC 3.1.3.2 binds the two-consent rule on every consensus_protocol; under open:self_admit one signature admits.

note: The policy row community_remove carries no floor cell and no cancel cell; the text puts every removal under the floor of two voices.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: Unanimity is what that ceremony gathers, and any change to the charter or the roster takes it.
side_b: CC 4.2.6: The bias gradient is **fire (one live survivor) ≤ roster change (a majority of the standing roster)**.
note: A roster change takes every holder under CC 5.3.4 (fresh genesis) and a strict majority of the standing roster under CC 4.2.6; governance_policy.tsv accord_majority ('every other accord threshold but the fire') follows CC 4.2.6. A lost or refusing holder blocks the change under one and not the other.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**
side_b: CC 2.6.8 a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains
note: CC 2.3.2.1 limits the check to the two proof-of-possession doors and keeps a held key under a non-matching id; CC 2.6.8 binds every resolution, which refuses that held key. CC 2.6.8 then says a collision is "detected at registration and never at resolution", agreeing with 2.3.2.1 against its own MUST.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "a retroactive identity claim that promotes a canonical hash to a real `key_id`, which opens rule 2"
side_b: CC 3.3.14: "it does not admit a `withdraws` from `K` against a target naming `H`"
note: Whether a key that has bound itself to a canonical hash may withdraw rows naming that hash. CC 2.4.1.1 says the binding opens rule 2; CC 3.3.14 says the binding admits nothing and the route is the rule-3 proxy.

side_a: CC 3.2 halt, notify, drill, resumption, root conferral, pipeline blessing, the amendment sign-off and entrenched ratification
side_b: CC 4.2.1 the agent text manifest statement of [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2); and
note: CC 3.2 restates the closed list of accord powers without the confirmation (accord:lifecycle:confirmed), the agent text manifest statement and the AccordCarrier announcement that CC 4.2.1 lists. A reader of 3.2 alone takes those three as outside the accord's role. CC 4.2.1 is the home.

side_b: CC 4.2.3 consensus_protocol_entrenched: true // replacement runs the CC 4.2.6 roster-change ceremony
note: Two copies of one family record cite two sections for the replacement of a holder. CC 4.2.1 holds no replacement ceremony (its ceremonies confer a root and bless a pipeline); CC 4.2.6 holds the roster change. The member keys also differ in form (quoted placeholders against bracketed names).

side_a: CC 4.5.13: "It is what every window in this document runs from (the window clock above)."
side_b: CC 2.6.7: "The substrate MUST refuse such a row whose `asserted_at` precedes the receiver's clock by more than `W`"
note: CC 4.5.13 says every window runs from the node's first-held instant. The freshness window W runs from the signer's asserted_at, the attach window from a cosignature's signed_at (CC 3.2 T4a), a membership proposal's 30 days from its asserted_at (constants.tsv). "Every window" is true of decision windows only; a reader of CC 4.5.13 alone times the others from receipt.

side_a: CC 3.2: "The receiver checks, in this order and before any cryptography: a per-sender-key rate, a per-link rate, then a node-wide ceiling on pending requests"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.5: "the three receiver rates (per-link, per-sender and node-wide) run before it as a set and not a sequence"
note: An order in CC 3.2 (sender, link, node-wide) and in CC 5.4.6 ("the receiver order"); "a set and not a sequence" in CC 5.3.3.5, which still requires that a frame refused per-link or per-sender spend no node-wide budget, an order in effect. The two also list link and sender in opposite order; the outcome agrees if node-wide is charged last.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: "Admission refuses shape only (`trust_accepts_classes_malformed`, `trust_accepts_depth_out_of_range`)."
side_b: CC 3.2: "The substrate MUST refuse to write the edge with `trust_root_head_stale` when the counted cosignatures are older than the window"
note: Both sentences are about admitting a trust:accepts edge. CC 4.4.3.8 says admission refuses shape only; CC 3.2 T4a adds three refusals on the head (stale, unwitnessed, unnamed) at first admission. The CC 4.4.3.8 sentence is about its two members and reads wider than that.

side_a: CC 4.5.1.3: "SHOULD return a `409 IDEMPOTENT_CONFLICT` with an advisory hint, NOT a hard reject"
side_b: CC 5.3.6.1: "Replay detected (e.g., duplicate `(tree_size, witness_key_id)` cosignature with different signatures)"
note: One status code for two things: an advisory about a near-duplicate value after which "the producer may proceed", and a detected replay. A 409 is a refusal on the wire, so whether the near-duplicate row was admitted is not stated; a client cannot tell the advisory from the conflict.

side_a: CC 7.3.5: The Wise Authority adjudicates only the federation's own deferrals and in-federation objections
side_b: CC 7.5.3: Regulatory revocation or WA injunction.
note: 'Only' deferrals and objections, and 'adjudication only' on the CC 4.5.1 register (no halt), against powers Part 7 gives a Wise Authority that are neither: an injunction that opens a sunset assessment (CC 7.5.3), a 'WA mandate' that triggers an emergency shutdown (CC 7.5.2 class B), approval that opens the sealed retirement logs (CC 7.5.5), an objection to a custodian (CC 7.5.7), mandatory sign-off at tier 5 (CC 7.3.3). CC 7.3.6 'WA oversight upholds the duties of creation' is broader again.

side_a: CC 7.1.4: Any ambiguous case → trigger WBD
side_b: CC 1.9: Uncertainty above deployment-defined thresholds.
note: CC 1.9 is the one statement of the triggers (three, the first a deployment threshold); CC 7.1.4 defers on any ambiguity, with no threshold. An agent built from CC 7.1.4 defers far more often. CC 1.16.4 says the triggers are those of CC 1.9.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: while WBD deferral is mandatory and freezes the deferring agent
side_b: CC 1.9: Await guidance; remain inactive on that issue.
note: The register cell (and CC 4.3 'it freezes the agent') stops the agent; CC 1.9 stops one action and leaves the agent working on everything else. CC 1.9 is the home. C234 records the same looseness in CC 1.16.4.

side_a: CC 7.3.4: an entrenched act of the trust root's holders that none has yet taken
side_b: CC 1.13.2: That recognition would be an **act of the HUMANITY_ACCORD under the first-contact discipline**
note: The path out of stewardship is an act of the HUMANITY_ACCORD in CC 1.13.2 and CC 4.5.1, and of 'the trust root's holders' in CC 7.3.4. Under the CC 1 reading rule an instance's own root has its own holders, so the two name different actors for an agent rooted elsewhere. CC 4.5.1 adds that the act is 'not yet defined'.

side_a: CC 1.15.5: Governance & Oversight: Require authorised review for changes to ethical logic.
side_b: CC 1.16.6: Governed Evolution - any change to core ethical logic requires WA sign-off.
note: Three deciders for one change: an unnamed authorised reviewer, a Wise Authority sign-off, and (CC 4.5.1, before the scale gate) the steward alone with the WA quorum 'deferred to mechanization'. A reader of CC 1.16.6 blocks a change the steward has decided until a WA signs.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.1.1: the federation cell's pool is sized to make `cell_pool ≥ min_pool(federation)` always true at federation genesis.
side_b: CC 4.5.1: Below that scale the machinery is theater, not protection.
note: CC 4.4.3.1.1 has the amendment route run through a federation WA pool that holds from genesis, and a shortfall is a constitutional crisis only the halt resolves; CC 4.5.1 defers the WA-quorum machinery until the scale gate and has the steward decide. Before the gate one reader requires a seated pool and the other requires none.

side_a: CC 4.2.3: The entrenchment property is what prevents any federation-internal authority from amending the protocol.
side_b: CC 4.2.6: Before the scale gate, the steward's authority over entrenched surfaces applies ([CC 4.5.1](#4.5.1))
note: CC 4.2.3 states the bar without exception; CC 4.2.6 and CC 4.5.1.2 state that before the scale gate the steward may change the entrenched accord surface. The exception is the document's rule; CC 4.2.3 omits it.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: A provisional row pins the chosen authority from the first admitted row, so the fallback never decides.
side_b: CC 4.5.1: Rule-layer changes (new prefixes, new envelope fields, new policies, calibration package version transitions) route through:
note: CC 3.1.7 has a producer land a provisional registry row in its own change and rows admit under it before ratification; CC 4.5.1 and CC 1.2 route every new prefix through the five steps and the four-test gate first. Before the scale gate both end at the steward, so the outcomes meet; after it they do not.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2: "The announce app-data MAY carry it for self-authenticating discovery, and the directory holds it as the durable source of truth."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.5: "each holding only the other's announce, which cannot carry a post-quantum pair"
note: CC 3.3.6.2 lets an announce carry the signed transport_destination occurrence, which is the row that publishes the transit pair; CC 5.3.3.5 says an announce cannot carry a post-quantum pair and builds the pre-seal route fetch on that. A dialler may or may not expect the signed row in app-data. The route fetch is the later and the more detailed.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "NO per-invitation / per-resolution directory query is emitted."
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "Phone-class peers that cannot hold the full directory resolve through their L1-relay parent over a relay-blinded path."
note: Adjacent bullets: no resolution query at all, then a phone that resolves by asking its parent. The fail-secure paragraph also forbids "a per-destination query". The section later names relay-blinded resolution as sanctioned, so the phone path is an exception the first bullet does not state.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "reaches it by **pull anti-entropy** on the one replication carrier — never by push, and never waiting on a user's action"

side_a: CC 5.2 "the substrate MUST NOT emit any holding claim observable outside the cohort"
side_b: CC 5.2 "The holding claims of `community` and `affiliations` content reach the roster's members only, in the same way."

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.3 "`tier = federation ⟹ hybrid signature present`"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "A row that is not federation-tier is never proxied, since a proxy cannot pull what it is not audience to"

side_a: CC 3.2: With no live *external* trust root, a substrate MUST disable federated agent capabilities and manifest validation, server-tier and fail-closed.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: With no valid *external* trust root, federated agent capabilities and manifest validation MUST be disabled at the server tier.

side_a: CC 1.7: It also holds 6 `consensus_protocol` kinds, the [CC 3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.4) reserved-prefix taxonomy

side_b: CC 1.7: 13 composition policies (A–M, [CC 4.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4)) and 5 canonicalization families
note: The two lists are not the same list: CC 2.6.9.1 adds the CC 3.5 relation precedence and the CC 5.3 endpoint shapes, which CC 1.7 does not name, and omits the consensus_protocol kinds CC 1.7 names; neither names the Part 6 pin-normative preimages whose vectors CC 6.1.4 calls the freeze gate.
