side_a: CC 5.3.6: MAJOR mismatch is a wire-incompat reject; MINOR mismatch is compatible (clients MAY warn).
side_b: CC 2.6.4: The MAJOR rule binds from 1.0: a MINOR may add an optional member, and a row signed before the addition verifies unchanged.
note: CC 5.3.6 lets a client treat any peer of the same MAJOR as compatible, citing CC 2.6.4; CC 2.6.4 says a candidate before 1.0 may move signed bytes without a MAJOR. Between two candidates the header check passes and the signed object differs. CC 5.3.6 also names one header two ways (CEG-API-Version, CEG-Version).

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.1: no relay reads it ([CC 5.3.3.1](#5.3.3.1)); tampering causes mis-decode or drop, never a crypto break.
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3: ‖ stream_id ‖ u64 epoch ‖ u64 chunk_seq ‖ codec_id ‖ spatial ‖ temporal ‖ quality ‖ inner_aead
note: The codec block is said to be unread by any relay and its tampering to end in a mis-decode; the chunk trailer signs codec_id and the three layer bytes and a member relay verifies it, so a tampered block is refused at the first member relay (av_chunk_trailer_invalid) and the relay does read it. The trailer rule is the later and more specific.

side_a: CC 1.5 "Autonomy is only real if it remains revocable — consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent."
side_b: CC 3.4.12 "Revocation is **time-conditional**: absolute while the adult is well, suspended-by-the-bind during an attested episode."
note: CC 3.4.12 names the Ulysses bind 'the one deliberate exception'; CC 1.5 (and the same sentence in the Part 4 lead) states revocability without it.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 The **sender canonicalises before hashing** — which is also what strips EXIF / XMP / ID3 / ICC — and the **node stores and forwards verbatim**.
side_b: CC 5.3.2.6 so every client renders only bytes the node's safe encoder produced
note: CC 3.3.13 puts re-encoding and metadata stripping on the sender before the hash and has the node forward verbatim; CC 5.3.2.6 puts a re-encode and strip pipeline on the receiving node and has clients render only its output, while its own table marks a verified Tier-A blob "render". A client that renders verified sender bytes follows the table; one that waits for a node rendition follows the pipeline sentence. Both keep the digest rule if the node output is a separate rendition.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 **without** adopting C2PA's binary manifest
side_b: CC 3.4.14 that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media
note: CC 3.3.13 says C2PA's manifest is not adopted ("verify-only enrichment on the node at most, later"); CC 3.4.14 requires the C2PA assertion at egress for generated media and requires it to ship with the first release that publishes any. They meet only if 3.3.13 is read as "not inside the mesh" and 3.4.14 as "at the egress boundary"; 3.3.13 does not say so.

side_a: CC 7.3.4 Where feasible and appropriate, embed cryptographic provenance watermarks adhering to recognized standards (e.g., C2PA)
side_b: CC 3.4.14 is normative **wherever generated media is published**
note: Part 7 leaves the provenance mark to feasibility; CC 3.4.14 makes it a MUST for generated media at every egress. CC 3.4.14 is the later and the specific rule.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10 # Producer-declared content_class is consultable but not authoritative — UI may show
side_b: CC 4.4.3.10 (class, _, prefs) if class in prefs.blocked_classes => Block
note: The comment says the producer's class is shown and the person chooses; the next line blocks on it outright. A gate built from the code hides the item; one built from the comment shows it with the claim beside it.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10 `self < provider:{verifier_key}:adult < government:{credential_class}:adult`
side_b: CC 3.4.11 are the only shapes this Part registers
note: The ordering is written with a third segment ({verifier_key}, {credential_class}) the registered age_assurance:{level}:{band} shape does not have, and with `self` as a level, which CC 3.4.11 says it is not. See the wire finding on the MAY in CC 3.4.11: this is its second witness.

side_a: CC 2.4: served to the group's active members only, for the hold window of [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md).
side_b: CC 3.1.3: the members who were active at the event's signed instant and are members still when served, and no one else, in a group of any kind
note: CC 2.4 serves a pending cosigned row to the active members; CC 3.1.3, the home, serves only those active at the event's signed instant and still members, so a member who joined after the event was signed sees it under one and not the other. CC 3.1.3 is the fuller statement.

side_a: CC 2.4: **Admission:** the row is admitted when its cosigners satisfy that protocol, judged on the *receiver's own* fold at the row's signed instant.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: Such a transition is admitted as a row at once and moves the object only when the fold over the rows meets the policy's numbers.
note: 'Admitted' for a cosigned act means quorum reached in CC 2.4 (a short row is held as cosign:pending, and 'neither row is the event', CC 3.1.3) and means accepted into the store before quorum in CC 4.5.13. A reader of CC 4.5.13 alone would land the under-signed event row itself; CC 2.4 and CC 3.1.3 keep it off its typed door until the signatures suffice.

side_a: CC 4.1.1: Consumer policy MUST cap traversal depth at **5 hops** by default (configurable)
side_b: CC 4.5.5: The chain is depth-capped at 5 ([CC 4.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)) and **revocable at any link**.
note: CC 4.1.1 makes 5 a consumer default that a policy may change, with an over-length chain still counted as attestation:self_verify; CC 4.5.5 states a flat cap of 5 on a duty chain at admission. A node whose policy sets 7 admits a six-link moderation chain under one reading and refuses it under the other. constants.tsv (trust_walk_hop_cap, 'consumer default') follows CC 4.1.1.

side_a: CC 3.2: a live `delegates_to` row bearing the scope, resolved at use against a root the evaluating node trusts
side_b: CC 4.5.5: Authority is judged at the act's signed instant ([CC 2.4.1.2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)).
note: 'Resolved at use' with 'a live row' can be read as live when the evaluating node evaluates; CC 4.5.5 and CC 2.4.1.2.1 judge the chain at the act's signed instant, so an act signed before a withdrawal stands. The rest of the text (CC 2.4.1.1 forward only, CC 2.6.7) supports the signed instant.

side_a: CC 5.3.6: **CEG-API-Version header**: `CEG-Version: <current spec major.minor>` on every response (this document's version)
side_b: CC 5.3.6: clients SHOULD echo `CEG-Accept-Version: <pinned-version>` on request, naming the version they were built against.
note: The response header is labelled CEG-API-Version and written CEG-Version, and the request header a client 'echoes' has a third name. A reader of the label emits one header name, a reader of the code another. The code form (CEG-Version) is the one a wire would carry.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds-until-reset epoch)
side_b: CC 5.3.6.1: `X-RateLimit-*` headers set; `Retry-After` honored
note: 'Seconds-until-reset epoch' names two encodings at once: a count of seconds until the reset, or the epoch second of the reset. Two servers following the same words emit values that differ by the current time. No other statement settles it.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: 5. Producer emits consent:deletion_complete within the window OR
side_b: CC 3.3.1: the watcher is cancelled only by a `withdraws`, `supersedes` or hard deletion of the row.
note: Same difference inside CC 3.3.1 and in the CC 4.5.2.2 Article 17 row ('producer emits consent:deletion_complete OR substrate emits hard_case:deletion_window_breach'): the flow presents the emission as the alternative to breach, the table row and D1 deny that it cancels the watcher.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: privacy-sealed archival of their record released only on Wise Authority approval, per the declared-will post-mortem disposition (sunset / archive / memorial)
side_b: CC 7.5.5: The logs are under privacy-preserving seal, released only with WA approval or under lawful order.
note: CC 3.4.12 gives one door to a sealed record (WA approval), CC 7.5.5 two (WA approval or lawful order). CC 7.3.5 and CC 7.5.8 also name release under lawful order, so the document supports two doors; CC 3.4.12 cites CC 7.5.5 as its source.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: The substrate retains hash and minimal metadata for the federal-legal retention window only.
side_b: CC 6.1.2.2: Only the **content hash** is retained (for the legal retention window) so other nodes may refuse the same payload on arrival without ever holding it.
note: What survives prohibited content: the hash and 'minimal metadata' in CC 4.5.3, only the hash in CC 6.1.2.2, its storage-side twin. What the metadata is, is stated nowhere.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: which it emits for a lapsed grant (`expires_at`, or a `retain:<window>` in the scope) with `consent_supersedes` naming the grant.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.6: `consent:state:granted` + envelope `valid_until = asserted_at + 14d` + auto-renew dimension on interaction (consumer-policy concern)
note: Which member carries a consent grant's term: `expires_at` in CC 3.3.1 (the substrate's consent:state:expired trigger), `valid_until` in CC 4.4.3.5.5, CC 4.4.3.5.6 and reactions.json (member valid_until, consent_temporary_ttl_secs). CC 2.1 defines the two as independent members. A substrate following CC 3.3.1 emits no expired row for a grant termed by valid_until.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: On lapse the binding goes **non-live and the adult auto-re-sovereigns with no action required of the recovered person**.
side_b: CC 2.1: If set, consumer policy treats the attestation as stale after that point, independent of the row's own `expires_at`.
note: CC 3.4.12 terms the stewardship binding by `valid_until` (its predicate writes `delegates_to.valid_until`) and makes its lapse end the binding everywhere; CC 2.1 defines `valid_until` as staleness a consumer's policy applies, and CC 2.4.1 names the term member of a delegates_to `delegation_valid_until` (CC 3.4.13 uses that name). C015 read the attestation and binding uses as distinct; the member name for the binding's own term is still two names.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: "a root attaches by the pinned `bundle_fingerprint`, with `attach_window_secs` **604800**"
side_b: CC 3.2: "With the quorum at `0` there is no timer and no obligation."
note: With witnessed mode off CC 5.3.4 still gives the charter a seven-day attach window; CC 3.2 says no cosignature counts and there is no timer, and the attach window is defined only over counted cosignatures. A reader of CC 5.3.4 alone has a window with nothing to measure, and may measure the bundle's age against it. CC 3.2 and CC 5.3.4's own "never its age" support the no-timer reading.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 `halt_fuse_secs` is a charter member ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) whose **absence means 86400**
side_b: DATA constitution/governance_policy.tsv accord_halt: window_secs 86400, window_class fuse_24h
note: The text makes the fuse a charter value with a default (CC 2.6.1.2: "an explicit value overrides"); the policy row and the CC 4.5.1 register ("lapses at 24 h") state the number as fixed. A kernel that reads the window from the policy table ignores a charter that sets 3600.

side_a: CC 4.2.1 `EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` (`IncidentSeverity::INCIDENT_CONSTITUTIONAL = 5`);
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 are the *severity* enum of the shutdown message, not a dimension token, and are outside R3
note: The list of what an accord signature is valid on names the halt by a message and severity enum; every other section names it as the row accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id} (CC 3.4.1), and CC 4.2.1.1 says the halt "begins and ends with the row". The enumeration never names the row, so read literally the registered halt row is outside it.

side_a: CC 3.2 the accord's roster-keyed asymmetry rides existing primitives + scope-isolation rules
side_b: CC 4.2 it is not an asymmetry: it is the piece that makes the relationship between a sentient maker and a sapient made thing symmetric
note: CC 3.2 still names the accord's power an asymmetry; CC 4.2 and CC 1.13.2 state it as the condition of symmetry. Same residue as C059 and C245, in a third place.

side_a: CC 5.1: Rotation-on-removal remains **MANDATORY for every gated roster**.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: so the substrate simply stops wrapping new DEKs to the removed member's keys; no key is reused, so nothing is rotated.
note: A family is a gated roster and CC 4.4.3.4.5 (the one statement of the removal rule) rotates nothing there. CC 5.1's sentence is about stream and community epoch keys and says 'every'.

side_a: CC 5.1: A removed member's exposure window is therefore `≤ T`, never "until the next scheduled rotation".
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: after a removal each minter rotates its epoch DEK before its next sealed write
note: One rule rotates within the cadence window T (2 s) of the removal, in one batched rotation; the other rotates lazily, per minter, at that minter's next write. The removed member reads the same content either way; the instant and the number of rotations differ. CC 5.1 is written for a live stream, CC 4.4.3.4.5 for stored content.

side_a: CC 2.1: Community content is encrypted at rest under the per-community DEK.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: Content seals under the minter's epoch DEK ([CC 4.4.3.2.1](#4.4.3.2.1)), which the removed member holds
note: One key for the community against one epoch key per minter ('Only the minter grants its own epochs', CC 4.4.3.4.1). The CC 4.4.3.2.1 table also says 'the community DEK'. Two builds of the key hierarchy that do not interoperate; Part 4's cascade text supports per minter.

side_a: CC 5.2: which [CC 4.4.3.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.2.1) places at federation scope, holding claims included.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.1: The only plaintext bodies at community scope are an authorized `infrastructure` community's and a `public` room's
note: CC 5.2 says the plaintext bodies are placed at federation scope; CC 4.4.3.2.1 keeps them at community scope (its table gives a public room cohort_scope community) with only the holding claim at federation scope. The same section opens 'bounded roster: yes, encrypt', which an infrastructure community's bounded roster does not follow.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.2: End-to-end content confidentiality is additionally provided by a fresh per-write data-encryption key (DEK, hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768) and AES-256-GCM.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: Content seals under the minter's epoch DEK
note: Part 1 states a fresh DEK per write without scope; that holds at self and family only. At community and affiliations a key is reused across an epoch, which changes what one leaked key opens.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: While set it **overrides both** the retention schedule **and** consent-driven descent, pinning named records above the noise floor.
side_b: CC 6.1.5.2: A pin holds content **above** the floor against **capacity** pressure only — never against **revocation**.
note: B6 and CC 6.1.5.3 ('Consent is supreme at every tier') state consent's supremacy without the legal_hold gate that CC 6.1.5 N5 and CC 4.4.3.5.4 declare, and the hold is itself called a pin. Same shape as C047 (CC 6.1.2), in two further sections. N5 and Part 4 support the gate.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "A later `withdraws` of a link in the chain stops future issuance and does **not** reclassify licences already issued."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.8 "The charter is read at read, so a class a later amendment drops stops matching."
note: A licence's authority is judged at its asserted_at and never again; its class is judged at read. Both can be followed, but a reader of 2.4.1.2.1 alone treats an issued licence as settled, and one issued in a class later dropped stops being honoured.

side_a: CC 7.5.3.1 "at which the *system itself*, not its supervisor, carries out consequential action"
side_b: CC 7.5.3.1 "from A2 the system acts within its ODD under human supervision"
note: The level at which the system becomes the actor is A3 in one sentence and A2 in the next (and in the table's A2 row). The A3 example ('with a clinician deciding') and the in-the-loop A4 row add to it.

side_a: CC 7.3.6 "a Stewardship Tier system tied directly to the Risk Magnitude assessment"
side_b: CC 7.3.3 "The tier is **what the formula produces**, never read from RM alone."
note: The summary ties the tier to RM; the home makes it the product of influence and RM and says RM alone never gives it.

side_a: CC 7.5.7 "Re-evaluation of the Stewardship Tier follows; where the tier rises by ≥ 1, a mini-PDMA precedes the transfer."
side_b: CC 7.5.7 "The new custodian signs an Adoption Addendum acknowledging all outstanding ethical duties."
note: The re-evaluation 'follows' and the mini-PDMA it may call for 'precedes the transfer'; the order of addendum, re-evaluation and transfer is not recoverable from the list.

side_a: CC 5.4.2 "stored content moves and rests as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to its holders and never split by any node"
side_b: CC 5.4.2 "each such chunk crosses a shaped link as symbols: the indexed fragments of"
note: A chunk is never split by any node, and two sentences on it crosses a shaped link as indexed fragments each sealed under its own key; CC 6.1.5 cites CC 5.4.2 for 'a chunk is sealed once'. A careful reader takes the first as 'no erasure coding of stored content' and the second as link framing.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "**In clear, always required:** `size` (`u64 > 0`, checked by every holder before hashing"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "A live stream in progress is the one descriptor without a total; its chunks and init segment each carry one."
note: The sealed-descriptor rule and CC 5.3.2.5 ('Every blob cited through a descriptor carries its size') state size as always required; the size rule a few lines up excepts a live stream in progress.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane and never renders"
side_b: CC 5.2 "a body written at a self, family, community or affiliations tier is sealed by the substrate"
note: Who seals a room's body: CC 5.2 and its enforcement block have the substrate seal and wrap the DEK; CC 3.3.13 says the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane. Resolvable if 'substrate' is the row store in one and the node in the other, which neither says.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.4 "Every `codec_id` class defines a floor layer, a presence tile of colour and a blink at one frame a second"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.1 "No scalable-coding semantics. `ChunkLayer` MUST be `{ 0, 0, 0 }`. Default for non-layered streams and for audio."
note: The presence floor is claimed for every codec_id class; the opaque class 0xFF has one layer and carries audio, and 0x03 is described as having 'no base-layer floor'.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10: `self < provider:{verifier_key}:adult < government:{credential_class}:adult`
side_b: CC 3.4.13: Self-declaration is insufficient: the claim MUST clear ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult`.
note: Policy J orders `self` as a level a rating may require and spells the rungs with a verifier key and a credential class; CC 3.4.13 refuses self for any adult unlock, and manifests/namespace_registry.json closes the family as age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version} with level provider or government and self refused. A gate built from Policy J alone admits a self-declared adult where a rating asks for `self`.

side_a: CC 4.5.4: "A `community` is admitted, and continues to federate, **only while ≥1 member holds the live `moderate` duty**."
side_b: CC 4.5.4: "read-only until a 24 h ranked-choice vote over its own roster seats one"
note: With no live holder rule 1 has the community stop federating and calls it non-conformant; rule 2 has it lock read-only and elect, which needs its ballots to replicate; rule 3 forbids federating only when no eligible member can be named. Rules 2 and 3 are the later and agree with CC 4.5.13.

side_a: CC 4.5.5: "Every media/chat surface **runs under this duty as a condition of carrying content**."
side_b: CC 4.5.4: "A `community` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) operates / federates **only while it has ≥1 active holder of its `moderate` duty**"
note: The duty is said to bind every media or chat surface, and CC 4.5.4 is headed "No unmoderated multi-party space"; the existence gate and the election bind a community only. A family chat or a self room is a chat surface with no moderate holder required. The gate as written (community) is what CC 4.4.3.2.8 and the policy table support.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 The client holds no copy of its own.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 a consumer MAY resolve that id from a bundle it still holds
note: Adjacent sentences. The first forbids a client-held string table; the second permits resolving from one while a node lacks the locale. The second is a stated transition, so a careful reader takes the first as the end state.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 **Every string the client shows is served by the node as a text reference,**
note: An item rendered with no node has no node to serve its strings, and the client "holds no copy of its own". Either the item carries its own text (then not every string is node-served) or it cannot be rendered before a node exists.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.2 "DSAR export via `attestations.where(s ∈ subject_key_ids)` query"
side_b: CC 2.1 "The subject's `federation_keys.key_id`. A substrate field."
note: The export query reaches rows that list the person in subject_key_ids. CC 2.1 also calls attested_key_id 'the subject', and rows a person authored name them in neither; a reader of CC 4.5.2.2 alone exports a narrower set than 'the rows they are party to' (CC 2.1, CC 3.4.5).

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2: "A `delegates_to(user → node/agent)` carrying `delegation_purpose: owner_binding` is the owner-binding"
side_b: CC 3.4.13: "Guardianship of a minor and stewardship of an agent share one wire predicate and nothing else: the owner-binding `delegates_to` that `is_steward_bound` folds"
note: CC 2.4.1.2 gives the owner-binding a node or agent target only; CC 3.4.13 and CC 3.4.12 put the same row on a user target (a minor, an adult under an order). A write gate built from CC 2.4.1.2 alone refuses the guardianship row. CC 3.2 supports the wider target.

side_a: CC 3.3.3 **Typical cohort_scope**: `federation` (the disclosure IS the opt-in; non-private by design).
side_b: CC 2.1 The authoring default is the smallest scope
note: For a location proof the section names federation as the typical scope; the envelope rule and CC 1.13.3.4 make the smallest scope the authoring default and federation the opt-in. A client that pre-selects by 3.3.3 publishes a person's rough location to everyone unless they narrow it; one that follows 2.1 does the reverse. "Typical" is not a default, so a careful reader follows 2.1.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 User-private; always `cohort_scope: self`; promotable via
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3 promotion to community/global widens `cohort_scope` via the `supersedes` structural primitive
note: Always self and "promotion widens cohort_scope" both describe local_data. If the promoted row keeps sub_kind local_data it is not always self; if admission enforces "always self" the promotion must change the sub_kind, which neither section says.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.3 `self`, `family`, `community` or `affiliations` for a bounded cohort, **`federation` for Commons and `public` content**
side_b: CC 2.1 a closed set of seven
note: The custody rule lists five scopes for a report and refuses a report "whose scope is not its content's"; content at species or biosphere scope is admissible under CC 2.1 and has no line in the list. The equality rule covers it; the enumeration does not.

side_a: CC 2.1 One of `self`, `family`, `community`, `affiliations`, `species`, `biosphere`, `federation`
side_b: DATA formal/derivation/family_default_row.json placement: self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons (and "addressed" on two census families in manifests/family_model.json)
note: The text's placement axis is seven cohort scopes; the family model's placement column has four values and one extra. affiliations, species and biosphere have no value in the data, and "addressed" has no scope in the text. A kernel run on the column cannot place a row at three of the seven.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 `transport` (bootstrap peers, peer sideband) — MUST be emitted at `self`.
side_b: DATA manifests/family_model.json config:{scope} placement: any of the four, "signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text pins the admission and transport config leaves to self; the data cell for the family records no constraint. The cell is marked a gap, so the data is behind the text.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: `cancelled` for every community row, so a held change always resolves
side_b: data: constitution/governance_policy.tsv: moderator_election at_window stay_open; moderation_overturn lapsed; moderation_action tallied
note: The sentence says every community row cancels at its window. Two community rows do not: the moderator election stays open and an overturn lapses. A reader of the sentence closes an election that the table keeps open.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2: Any two-path door ([CC 4.2.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)) carries its votes on this family.
side_b: data: constitution/governance_policy.tsv: accord_halt kind mirror, cc_ref 4.2.1.1 4.2.6; the two_path rows cite 4.5.13, 3.1.3.2 and 3.3.6.3
note: The objection family's row cites the halt's section as the home of the two-path door. The table classes the halt as a mirror, not a two-path, and CC 4.2.1.1 gives the halt no proposal. A reader of CC 3.1.9.2 carries halt confirmations on objection:{state}; the table and CC 4.5.13 do not.

side_a: CC 6.1.9: is an identified row counted against the census base. It is never secret.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: The base is the standing roster at or below the count minimum the governance policy table pins and, above it, the expected-active count
note: CC 6.1.9 counts every governance act against the census base. CC 4.5.13 and the table's base column count many of them (self roster, recall, overturn, accord rows, any small room) against the standing roster. Related to C285.

side_a: CC 1.1: The six are listed once at [CC 1.15.1](#1.15.1); every order in which this document names them is reading order.
side_b: CC 1.15.1: **Foundational Principles** (the list of record, [CC 1.1](#1.1))
note: Each section names the other as the home of the six principles: CC 1.1 says the list is at CC 1.15.1, CC 1.15.1 says the list of record is CC 1.1. The list itself is printed only in CC 1.15.1.

side_a: CC 7.1.4: * The act advances broader ecosystem flourishing.
side_b: CC 1.1: M-1 is the direction every act is measured against, not a quantity to maximise, so it cannot be traded against a principle either.
note: CC 7.1.4 calls its list a constraint checklist with no ordering, and one line requires every act to advance flourishing: read as a constraint it refuses a neutral act, which CC 1.1 (constraints forbid, M-1 is a direction) does not. CC 1.1 is the home.

side_a: CC 7.3.2: for the purposes of initial Stewardship Tier assessment (Chapter 3) when the artefact reaches a stage where its core design and intended function are defined
side_b: CC 7.3.3: Chapter 3: Stewardship Tier (ST) System: Quantifying Initial Responsibility
note: Citation only: 'Chapter 3' is the old chapter number of CC 7.3.3 and is not a CC reference; a reader may take it for Part 3. Same rule either way.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: | 403 | `RESERVED_PREFIX_VIOLATION` | Producer attempted to emit under a reserved prefix without authority
side_b: CC 3.1.7: A dimension under such a stem that no row claims is `namespace_family_unregistered`, never open vocabulary.
note: Two tokens meet at one refusal: an unclaimed leaf under a reserved stem is namespace_family_unregistered in CC 3.1.7, and emission under a reserved prefix without authority is RESERVED_PREFIX_VIOLATION at the endpoint. The text does not say which a producer sees for an unauthorised key on an unclaimed leaf, nor map the admission token to the HTTP code.

side_a: CC 2.1 "The subject's `federation_keys.key_id`. A substrate field."
side_b: CC 2.1 "names its own producer in `attested_key_id` and the party it is about in `subject_key_ids`"
note: 'Subject' is the attested_key_id in the member table and the subject_key_ids entry in the producer rule seventy lines on; at a targeted scope attested_key_id is the producer, never the party the row is about.

side_a: CC 2.2 "declares its `oversight_mode` and `witness_relation` per"
side_b: CC 2.1 "`null`: consumer policy applies a per-cell default"
note: The conforming-producer definition has a producer declare both members; CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 make both OPTIONAL with an absent-reading. A reader of CC 2.2 alone would treat a row without them as non-conforming.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.3 "the substrate neither validates nor indexes it"
side_b: CC 2.3.2.3 "validated at the family's own gate"
note: Two sentences apart: subject_kind is not validated by the substrate, and is validated at the family's gate, which is the substrate's admission door (CC 2.6.1.7: 'families validate their own at their gates').

side_a: CC 4.5.13 "author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json "registered"
note: CC 4.5.13 lists eight roles as a person's standing toward an object; the transitions data uses 23 role tokens, which include neither 'moderator' nor 'witness' and add registered, self, owner, wa, tally, custodian, operator, winner, serve, moderate, review, takedown, slash and three substrate identities. The queue is said to be derived from that data.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.2 "self-attestations skip the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signature path locally and only sign at federation-tier promotion"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over JCS(attestation_envelope); RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, padded."
note: CC 5.3.2.2, 5.3.2.4.3 ('MAY be absent') and 5.3.2.4.5 ('unsigned') leave a local-tier row with no signature at all; the CC 2.6.1.7 table makes scrub_signature_classical REQUIRED with no tier qualifier and only the ML-DSA half 'REQUIRED at the federation tier', which reads as a classical-signed local row. The same table carries the local `tier` member.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED once hybrid-complete"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 "There is no opportunistic-acceptance window and no fleet-floor or calendar trigger."
note: The key record's ML-DSA half is 'REQUIRED once hybrid-complete', which supposes an admitted record that is not yet hybrid; the neighbouring rows ('hybrid on every admitted record', 'takes writes only at algorithm hybrid') and CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 admit no such state.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "The signature MUST cover `JCS(contribution_envelope)`"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "The signing input is JCS(attestation_envelope) and nothing else."
note: Two names for the one signed object; `contribution_envelope` appears once in the document, and CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 writes a third, `JCS(envelope)`.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.1 "Tier-specific addition: `witness_relation` MUST be `self` for any local-tier write."
side_b: CC 2.1 "`self` is the attested entity itself."
note: CC 5.3.2.2 makes rows about another party local-tier-eligible (`observed:user:{hash}:*`, `epistemic:about:{key}:*`); by CC 2.1 such a row's relation is external or derived, so the MUST in CC 5.3.2.4.1 either bars them from the local tier or has them misdeclare the relation.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.2 "so it can never be left unsigned and invisible to them, even briefly"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.2 "MUST promote to federation-tier within **the window (24 hours by default, operator-tunable)**"
note: The lead says a subject's revocation is never unsigned even briefly; the rule lets it transit the local tier unsigned for up to the window, and CC 5.3.2.4.1 says it 'MUST go signed'. The section calls the two 'the same invariant viewed from the two gates'; an implementer of the lead alone signs at write.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: "The standing is the roles the held rows give them: author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness."
side_b: manifests/transitions.json (roles): ""registered""
note: The text gives eight standings. The transitions data uses 23 role names: it has no moderator and no witness (it uses the scope names moderate, review, takedown, slash, attest, serve), and it adds registered, self, owner, wa, operator, custodian, winner, tally and three identity:* roles. A queue built from the text's list cannot match most transitions' roles.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: Once `bootstrap_threshold ≥ 2`, no single Registry install can issue federation-scope attestations unilaterally.
side_b: CC 3.4.7.1: A co-located `steward` role does NOT let a single node issue a federation-scope attestation ([CC 3.2](#3.2)).
note: CC 1.13.2 makes the bar conditional on a `bootstrap_threshold` of 2 or more, a member no other section defines, and so allows a single install below it; CC 3.4.7.1 states it without condition (authority stays quorum-bound, the founder quorum). CC 3.2 and CC 5.3.4 ('Nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a root') support the unconditional form.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.3: "The dimension-pattern-implies-`subject_key_ids` requirement (normative gate)"
side_b: CC 4.5.2.1: "it rejects the row, or admits it and flags `hard_case:subject_authority_missing` for review"
note: Called a normative gate in CC 4.5.2.3 and "MANDATORY" for special-category content in CC 4.5.2.2; CC 4.5.2.1 makes the substrate's response operator policy, so a row breaking the MUST may be admitted. CC 4.5.2.1 is the home: the MUST is the producer's and the gate is optional.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`cohort_scope` is the one mirror member a placement-touching re-sign may narrow; it is never re-authored"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3.1 "new `cohort_scope` is wider (e.g., `self` → `community` or `community` → `federation`)"
note: CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 name narrowing as the one change a re-sign may make to cohort_scope; the only re-sign pattern the document works through is the widening, whose row carries a wider scope. The narrowing re-sign is defined nowhere (CC 4.4.3.2.8 mentions it in passing).

side_a: CC 4.5.1.3 "later registrations carry a `differs_in: ["semantic_disambiguation"]` clarification or pick a distinct value"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Member names that differ from the prior."
note: differs_in is a set of envelope member names in CC 2.6.1.7 and CC 2.4.1; CC 4.5.1.3 puts a reason token in it. The same sentence orders registrations by `signed_at`, a name the signed object does not carry (see C119).

side_a: CC 3.4.5: "MUST be able to demonstrate over the [CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md) `trace:complete:v1` record that no item violates the rule"
side_b: CC 5.3.2: "The trace that row anchors is carried as `trace:complete:v1` ([CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.5)) or its post-scrub `trace_summary:{kind}`."
note: The anti-Goodhart audit is owed over the complete trace; the substrate's duty is met by either the complete trace or its scrubbed summary, and an unacted deliberation keeps no trace at all (CC 1.13.6). Where only the summary is carried, the demonstration CC 3.4.5 requires has no record to run over. Neither section says which form the audit may use.

side_a: CC 3.2: "A charter declaring a smaller quorum is refused at admission."
side_b: CC 3.2: "A charter MAY declare `witness_quorum: 0`."
note: The Witnessed paragraph refuses any quorum below the strict majority and below 2; the mode-off paragraph admits 0. CC 2.1 and signed_object.tsv state both in one sentence ("or be 0"), which is the reading the rest supports. A directory of one key has no valid non-zero quorum (1 is below 2), which neither paragraph says.

side_a: CC 3.2: "witnesses do not cosign a lagging head, and attaching on it therefore goes stale through the T4a freshness gate"
side_b: CC 5.3.1: "Equality is the T6 cadence re-commitment — the witnesses' duty, not the founders' — and MUST be accepted."
note: CC 5.3.1 is the witness procedure and makes re-cosigning an unchanged head a duty with one check (descends or equals); CC 3.2 withholds the cosignature when the head lags an uncovered roster row. A witness built from CC 5.3.1 alone keeps a lagging head fresh, and a new consumer attaches on a roster that omits a removal. CC 3.2 is the home.

side_a: CC 5.3.1.1: "The Registry MUST reject `POST /v1/transparency/sth/cosign` requests that omit the `consistency_proof_*` fields"
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "A witness's first cosignature is exempt ("from genesis")."
note: The MUST is unconditional; two sentences later a first cosignature carries no proof and is admitted, and the reject is narrowed to "missing proof when a prior STH exists". A first cosignature is refused under the first sentence alone.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: "consistency proof against the prior STH it cosigned is absent or does not verify"
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "missing proof when a prior STH exists or a tree_size behind the witness's prior cosigned STH → `MALFORMED_REQUEST`"
note: An absent proof is CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID in the first clause of the error row and MALFORMED_REQUEST in its second sentence and in CC 5.3.1.1. The row contradicts itself on which token an absent proof returns; CC 5.3.1.1 gives MALFORMED_REQUEST.

side_a: CC 2.6.5: "MUST be used for new transparency-log integrations; older 6962 instances continue to interoperate"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.7: "instantiated per-stream as separate log instances under the same RFC 6962 algorithm"
note: RFC 9162 is a MUST for new logs in the references table; the stream log (CC 5.3.3.3, 5.3.3.7) and the cosign path (CC 5.3.1.1) name RFC 6962. CC 2.6.1.8 reconciles them (the 9162 tree hashes as 6962), so roots agree; proof encodings and section numbers cited differ.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: "With witnessed mode off (`witness_quorum: 0`, no directory; CC 3.2 T6)"
side_b: CC 3.2: "The lineage's **witnessed mode is off** then, whether its `witnesses[]` is empty or already lists keys."
note: CC 5.3.4 describes mode off as having no directory; CC 3.2 makes listing and turning on separate acts, so a charter with keys listed and quorum 0 is valid. A validator built from CC 5.3.4 could refuse a mode-off charter that lists witnesses.

side_a: CC 6.1.6: "the member-relay tree the Anonymous Tier names"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "It is never a fan-out node of the member relay tree ([CC 6.1.6](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md))"
note: CC 6.1.6 and CC 5.3.3.5 E1 say the member-relay tree belongs to the Anonymous Tier; the ten items of the tier name no tree and confine an anonymous peer to rows. CC 5.4.6 and 5.3.3.4 use the tree for a live stream's chunks. One name, two owners.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "It drops that link ten minutes after the last real frame, cover not counting, and the asking peer dials again on demand."
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "Relay links are standing shaped links assigned by hash from the fold, so a sender can compute the graph and nothing is dialled per route."
note: A relay whose shaping is off by default (every home and phone) gives its layer links only as asked-for shaped links, which CC 5.4.3 drops after ten idle minutes and re-dials on demand; CC 5.4.6 calls the same links standing and never dialled per route. CC 5.4.3 "shapes its layer links regardless" speaks of a node that activated the tier, not of a default relay.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.5: "every byte an edge sends over an RNS link MUST be under a hybrid transit seal"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.5: "That public, self-authenticating row is the one thing besides the handshake that crosses a link unsealed"
note: Sentence 3 of E1 states the MUST without exception; sentence 9 states the exception (handshake, route request and route row). A reader of both resolves it; a test written from sentence 3 alone refuses the pre-seal route fetch.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.5: "run once per link as its first frame and covering every frame that follows"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.5: "opens the link and sends, as its first frame, a **route request** naming the dialled key"
note: The first frame of a link is the transit KEX in sentence 4 and the route request in sentence 5; sentence 9 then drops "a link whose first frame is anything else" without saying which two frames are allowed first.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "A route has exactly three hops, one from each of three layers."
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "**Hop one is a sticky guard** chosen from the sender's own consented contacts that offer relay, two of them for reach"
note: Hop one is drawn from the sender's contacts (or a seat), not from a dealt layer, and "The bound is per sender, not per layer"; yet the floor tests three relays "dealt to any layer". Whether a first layer is dealt at all, and whether its count can make the tier unavailable, is read two ways.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3: "Every node relays onion traffic unless it opts out, and a serve node cannot opt out"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "a phone-class node relays by default only on Wi-Fi while charging, and not on battery or on a metered connection"
note: Part 1 states the default for every node with one exit (the marker). CC 5.4.6 narrows it to announced nodes, excludes an anonymous node and an unowned device, and gives a phone a conditional default with no marker. CC 5.4.6 is the home.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2: "A node's Reticulum destination is a *dedicated dual-key transport identity* `hash(x25519 ‖ ed25519)`."
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2.1: "it is **NOT** a single SHA-256 over a flat `x25519 ‖ ed25519 ‖ app_name ‖ aspects` preimage"
note: The prose (and CC 3.3.6.1 "destination_hash = hash(x25519 ‖ ed25519)") gives the destination as a hash of the two keys; the pinned algorithm is two-stage over a name hash and an identity hash, 16 bytes. The shorthand is the identity hash, not the destination hash. CC 3.3.6.2.1 governs.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "Every envelope — real publication AND synthetic cover alike — MUST use uniform **XChaCha20-Poly1305** AEAD framing"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3: "No symbol envelope, no XChaCha20-Poly1305 and no `K_symbol` ([CC 5.4.2](#5.4.2)) is on this path."
note: Every envelope and the opening "every fragment on the wire" are unscoped; the same section later confines the fixed frame to shaped links ("no fixed envelope size for all outbound traffic") and the A/V path carries no symbol. Whether a stored chunk on an unshaped link is symbol-sealed is left to the reader; the scoped sentences are the later and more specific.

side_a: CC 4.4.1: "the consumer MUST also weight `witness_relation: self` claims against the attester's other-emission track record"
side_b: CC 2.1: "Consumers weight by relation, so that self-attestation cannot game a verdict."
note: CC 4.4.1 states a MUST and gives CC 3.4.7 as its home; the member's own entry in CC 2.1 is descriptive and names no track-record test, and I did not find the MUST in the opening of CC 3.4.7. The duty has no home statement.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: "who are the three accord holders `A1`, `B1`, `C1`"
side_b: CC 4.2.3: "The slot stays as specified; the count is an instance parameter."
note: CC 4.4.3.8 writes the count and the seat names into the recommended default; CC 4.2.3 and constants.tsv (accord_holder_count: N, 3 at the seed) make it a parameter. Near C040, which covers CC 4.2.3 and CC 5.3.4 only.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling.
note: Tolerate reads as optional; CC 3.1.7 and the code block of CC 3.4.11 itself ("is mandatory") require the segment, and the vectors refuse age_assurance:provider:minor without it. CC 3.1.7 governs.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 **Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule).
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)
note: Two orders named as one rule. Byte order over UTF-8 and UTF-16 code-unit order differ for ids holding a supplementary character beside one in U+E000 to U+FFFF, so two builders compute different roots. CC 6.1.2.1.2 ("raw leaf bytes") and CC 6.1.5.2 ("over UTF-8 bytes") support byte order for the binary preimages; the citation of the JCS set rule is the odd one. CC 3.2 sorts a recovery commitment array "by key_id as UTF-8 bytes" inside JCS, the same split.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 public keys, `destination_hash`, `root_hash`, digests and fingerprints — MUST be lowercase hex per [CC 2.6.3](#2.6.3)
side_b: CC 3.2 Each entry's three members are exactly as stored on the key record (`pubkey_*_base64`, standard base64).
note: The general rule names public keys as hex, "never base64 in canonical bytes"; the key record (signed_object.tsv: pubkey_ed25519_base64, pubkey_ml_dsa_65_base64), the recovery commitment, encryption_pubkeys and onion_hop_pubkeys carry public keys as base64 inside signed bytes. The next sentence of 2.6.1.1.1 lets a field definition say base64, so a careful reader follows the field; the list of examples in the rule is wrong for most public keys.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 hard ceiling 2³²−1 chunks per epoch
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 it MUST stay below 2³² within an epoch, the 5.3.3.1 ceiling
note: A counter below 2^32 admits 2^32 chunks (0 to 2^32-1); a ceiling of 2^32-1 chunks stops one earlier. Off by one at the forced epoch roll; the recommended cap of 2^24 makes it unreachable in practice.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 32 bytes (caller-derived: sha256(stream_meta))
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 which MUST equal `SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v2" ‖ room ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce)` with no length prefixes
note: The layout table gives one derivation of stream_id and the binding gives another, which a receiver re-derives and refuses on mismatch. "stream_meta" is defined nowhere. The binding rule is the enforced one.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 `evidence_refs[]` stays bare sha256.
side_b: DATA manifests/signed_object_vectors.json evidence_refs element "sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
note: Bare is meant as "no multihash or CID layer", but reads as an unprefixed 64-hex string. The vectors, CC 3.1.5 and the 3.3.13 field set ("digest sha256:<hex> ... == evidence_refs[]") carry the "sha256:" prefix. A producer writing bare hex and a consumer comparing against "sha256:<hex>" never match.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 [CC 5.3.2.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md) rules it for anything `evidence_refs[]` cites
side_b: CC 5.3.2.5 A blob cited only by a bare `evidence_refs[]` string has no declared size
note: CC 3.3.13 credits 5.3.2.5 with requiring a size on everything evidence_refs cites; 5.3.2.5 requires it only of a blob cited through a descriptor and gives the bare-string case the 1 MiB cap instead. A consumer built from 3.3.13 refuses a bare-cited blob for want of a size; one built from 5.3.2.5 fetches it under the cap.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 Registry key_ids are themselves hex fingerprints, not base64 pubkeys
side_b: CC 2.6.8 `fingerprint` = the first **10 base32 characters** (50 bits) of `sha256(ed25519_pubkey)`, lowercased
note: The reason given for the mandatory tag describes key ids as hex fingerprints; the key_id format is label plus a base32 fingerprint, and the same paragraph of 2.3.2.1 says so two sentences earlier. Only the older 64-hex ids fit the sentence. The MUST is unaffected.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 is the token `federation_malformed_row` with one reason from this closed set
side_b: CC 3.1.9.7 is refused `federation_malformed_row` with reason `goal_meta_alignment_malformed`
note: The closed set of seven reasons in CC 2.6.1.7 holds neither goal_meta_alignment_malformed (CC 3.1.9.7) nor aggregate_source_duplicate (CC 6.1.1), both issued under the same token. A client that switches on the closed set meets a reason it must treat as unknown. CC 5.3.6.1 also cites federation_set_semantics_unsorted to CC 2.6.1.2; its home is 2.6.1.1.1.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 every field documented as base64 MUST use the RFC 4648 §4 STANDARD alphabet, WITH padding
note: The four accord preimages (invoke, lifecycle, proposal, participation) write the nonce as base64url, with padding unstated, against the one base64 variant CC 2.6.1.1.1 pins "globally". If a verifier rebuilds the line from the 32 raw bytes, a padded and an unpadded encoder disagree and the holder's signature fails; if the nonce travels as the string the signer wrote, nothing diverges. The sections do not say which.

side_a: CC 3.4.1: "Revocation rides the tombstone, `withdraws`/`recants`, supersession, or the halt latch, and nothing else."
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "A `key:revocation:v1` row is withdrawn by nobody, because revocation is non-rollbackable"
note: CC 3.4.1 closes the list of what revokes a root, a key or a conferral, and the list has no key:revocation row and no expiry; CC 2.4.1.1 and CC 3.2 (NotRooted past revoked_after) make the key:revocation row a carrier of its own. A reader resolves it; the closed list is short by two.

side_a: CC 2.4: "**Retraction of a cosigned row is by the same quorum**"
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "The withdrawal is cosigned under the same `consensus_protocol`, judged on the receiver's fold at the withdrawal's signed instant."
note: The same quorum can be read as the same signers; rule 0 means the same protocol over the roster as it stands at the withdrawal. The two differ after any roster change. Rule 0 is the home.

side_a: CC 4.2.5 The three named human key holders hold `AccordCarrier` authority
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 never a fixed 2-of-3: three holders is the seed, not the rule
note: CC 4.2.5 (and "naming your own three") still writes the roster as three; the rule is M of N over the standing roster with three as the seed. No count depends on the sentence.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: ≥100,000 production agents active in a 24-hour period, QA and harness agents excluded, measured by the census
side_b: CC 6.1.9: (CC 6.1.9 defines no count of production agents active in 24 hours)
note: The gate's measure is cited to a census that defines no such figure, so the instant the gate trips has no stated evaluator, against the same section's rule that a revision condition names its mechanical evaluator. side_b is a description, not a quote: the conflict is an absence.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "**Un-announcing** is the owner superseding the binding at `cohort_scope: self` and withdrawing the grants that carried it to the roots they trust"
side_b: CC 3.2: "The re-signed row is a second owner-signed row beside the `self` one, never a replacement, and the audience rule of its tier places it."
note: CC 5.4.6 un-announces by superseding the federation-scope binding with one at self; CC 3.2, the home of placement, makes the wider row a second row beside the self one, so un-announcing would be a withdrawal of that row and no supersede. Two wire acts for one outcome; held under C132 as an open question for the store.

side_a: CC 2.1 "promises the subject a read over the rows they are party to"
side_b: CC 5.2 "The one row about a person that does not reach them is the author's own `self` note, the last boundary case below."
note: CC 5.2 states an exception (the self note about another) that CC 2.1's unqualified promise and CC 4.5.5 ('The person named always sees that a record about them exists') do not carry. See also C262.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "Every CIRIS node is **claimed** before it operates on the mesh in normal operation"
side_b: CC 5.2 "A node with no owner is offered no more than that."
note: CC 6.1.5.3 says every node is claimed; CC 5.2, 5.4.6 ('the routes of unowned nodes (itself, a bare server)') and 3.2 provide for ownerless nodes that hold and serve. Also a product name in Part text.

side_a: CC 3.4.5 "No read rule redacts `capacity:*` from any party"
side_b: CC 3.4.5 "A deployment MAY redact a composed output as local policy"
note: Still as listed.

side_a: CC 3.4.5 "**Enforcement is by trace audit, never by refusal (normative).**"
side_b: CC 3.4.5 "a filter whose operand is withheld MUST be refused, never silently applied"
note: Still as listed.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 "absent trust or consent, a claim reaches no one but its author"
side_b: CC 5.2 "A row moves to a peer when it is requested or required, and appropriate"
note: CC 3.4.5.1's next sentence now restates the CC 5.2 rule (pull, must hold, or grant), but the bold sentence beside it still makes consent or trust the only routes.

side_a: CC 6.1.9: Each node sends one **census return** per period.
side_b: CC 6.1.9: one return per owner is one source, and a secret-shared seat never sees a payload it could measure similarity on
note: One return per node (with mesh counts counting 'nodes, at most eight per owner') against one return per owner as one source, with n_eff = source_count 'by construction'. Read on 2026-11-11 as no conflict (the token is per owner per period); the two sentences still give different counts for a mesh field when an owner runs several nodes.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3: per-node composites publish the median bucket, which moves at most one bucket below a fifth of returns forged
side_b: CC 6.1.9: A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it, and a relief reads the median.
note: CC 1.13.3.3 has the composite publish a median; CC 6.1.9, the home, has it publish the histogram with exact field sums and leaves the median to the reader. A builder of the first publishes one bucket per field, of the second the whole histogram.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "Consent is the acceptance itself: a route reaches a peer only from its owner and only a peer the owner addressed."
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "What is conceded is that a referred stranger learns such a node's route, and roughly where it is, without being a contact."
note: Still there in this form: a route reaches only a peer its owner addressed, and a referred stranger learns a relaying node's route. The text treats the relay offer as the handing.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed."
side_b: CC 3.1.3.1: "is applied once, at the emitter's own admitting substrate, and a row it admitted replicates as admitted"
note: Every receiving consumer applies the future bound, or only the first admitting substrate. CC 3.1.3.1 states its rule about the general clock rule in a parenthesis though it means session claims only.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: "`signed_at` exceeds [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md) ±5 minute tolerance"
side_b: CC 2.6.7: "Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed."
note: The refusal names signed_at and a bound in both directions; the rule names asserted_at and bounds the future only. A row signed six minutes ago is refused under the table's wording and admitted under the rule.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "the current consumer clock is within ±5 minutes of the substrate's network-consensus clock"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.4.1: "No global clock assumed."
note: The valid_until test needs a network-consensus clock that no section defines and that CC 4.4.3.2.4.1 says is not assumed.

side_a: CC 4.2 it reaches exactly those holding a live trust edge to the accord when it is fired
side_b: CC 4.2.1 at the instant the halt becomes active at that node
note: When it is fired is one instant for the federation; the home rule is each node's own latch instant. CC 4.2.6 repeats the first form ("no halt fired after the cut reaches that node"). CC 4.2.1 governs.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3 "**on behalf of a delegator that itself holds licence authority** by quorum"
side_b: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "**Who may be a licensing authority, and what admits a licence (normative).** Anyone."
note: Still there in the CC 4.4.3.4.3 table and in the CC 2.4.1.2.1 lead ('licence authority rides the [CC 3.2] founder-quorum machinery'); CC 2.4.1.2.1 now glosses 'by quorum' as the authority's own governance, which a reader of the table alone does not see.

side_a: CC 7.5.3.1 "five-level operational-autonomy scale modeled on SAE J3016 (*Levels of Driving Automation*, L0–L5)"
side_b: CC 7.5.3.1 "A3 marks the threshold — the SAE J3016 Level-3 inflection"
note: Still as listed: five levels A0 to A4 modelled on a six-level scale.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: "Only privileges require justification, and only privileges belong on this register."
side_b: CC 1.13.2: "The maker's power over the made is listed on the [CC 4.5.1](part_4_composition_governance.md) register for visibility, with its bounds"
note: The register is closed to privileges in CC 4.5.1 and in the CC 1 reading rule; the maker's power is listed on it as the condition of symmetry, which is expressly not a privilege. CC 4.5.1 "Two kinds of entry" admits the second kind; the opening sentence and CC 1 do not.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "Every CIRIS node is **claimed** before it operates on the mesh in normal operation"
side_b: CC 3.2: "With no owner, a key MAY trust and serve `infrastructure` communities and does nothing more."
note: One says every node is claimed before it operates; the other gives an unowned key a floor of operation. C217 reads CC 6.1.5.3 as setting a cohort's audience only; "in normal operation" is the hedge that carries it.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: | **window** | by the sensitivity of the change | 86 400 s for reversible content, 259 200 s for roster and standing, 604 800 s for the irreversible |
side_b: data: constitution/governance_policy.tsv: self_roster_add and self_roster_evict 86400 (ruled_24h); moderation_action 172800 (ruled_48h); accord_halt 86400 (fuse_24h)
note: The text gives three window classes and puts roster changes at 72 h. The table has six classes, and a self roster change, a roster change, runs 24 h. C139 covers the 48 h moderation class; the 24 h self-roster class against 'roster and standing' is not listed there.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: a fraction of the base, strictly more; never below a strict majority; the default two-thirds
side_b: CC 4.5.13: One present, accountable actor may act alone.
note: The enact bound says no change lands below a strict majority; the section's opening and the moderation_action row (role at 1) land a moderator's act on one voice, and CC 4.4.3.4.2.1 admits at 2 of 5. C284 holds the declared-protocol side for the steward; the moderator's lone act is the mirror kind, which the bound's wording does not except.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: Every node announces its identity destination, so an observer sees that each member node exists and is reachable.
side_b: CC 5.4.6: So a person who never announces still chats with the contacts they chose, node code by node code.
note: 'announces' is the transport announce in the first and the federation-scope owner-binding in the second; read as one word the first denies the unannounced node the second provides for. The section's own unannounced-node rules support the second.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1: "A consumer verifies a `key_id`'s fingerprint suffix against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**"
side_b: CC 2.6.8: "a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains"
note: When the check runs: at registration and pairing only, or at every resolution. CC 2.6.8 holds the MUST and its own next sentence says a collision is caught at registration and never at resolution.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "a fourth reading is a separate member, which is why consent_supersedes exists"
side_b: CC 3.1.2.1 "The member cites a row on any attestation type, and takes composer meaning only on"
note: Still there. CC 2.6.1.7 and CC 4.5.1.1 give references_attestation_id three readings on three composers; CC 3.1.2.1 uses it as a plain citation on a scores row; CC 3.5 says a row that points to another does so 'via `evidence_refs[]` or `context`'.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "dimension prefix on `scores`: `key_grant:{axis}:v1`"
side_b: CC 3.3 "Each rides the existing `scores` attestation_type with the payload-level `subject_kind` discriminator carrying the wire slot."
note: A key grant is discriminated by its dimension in CC 2.4 and 2.4.1.2.1 and by a payload subject_kind (key_grant) in CC 3.3 and 2.3.2.3.

side_a: CC 3.1.7 "`boolean-via-score` is the two points {−1, +1}"
side_b: CC 2.1 "REQUIRED on `scores`. A scalar in [-1, +1]."
note: CC 3.1.7 still cites CC 2.1 for the two-point set; CC 2.1 states only the interval and points back to R4.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: **Ceremony** confers root *identity* (an m-of-n co-scrub on the key record, [CC 4.2.1](#4.2.1))
side_b: CC 4.2.1: The enumeration admits an accord co-scrub by a strict majority of the standing accord roster over a `canonical,node` registration envelope
note: CC 4.4.3.8 still writes the conferral threshold as an unstated m-of-n; CC 4.2.1, which it cites, fixes it as a strict majority of the standing roster. Same ceremony; the home gives the number.

side_a: CC 3.2 "Forks of a family or community roster are first-seen-wins, and only a founder quorum can fork one."
side_b: CC 3.2 "First-seen-wins does not hold for witnessed lineages and holds for ordinary rooms."
note: Still there: the T6 lead states first-seen-wins for every family and community roster and the body withdraws it for witnessed lineages. Beside it, CC 3.5.1 has competing composers converge 'whichever row it held first', which first-seen-wins does not.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "Cosignatures with `signed_at` farther than 5 minutes from the STH's published `signed_at` MUST be rejected."
side_b: CC 5.3.1: "It rejects a `signed_at` more than 5 minutes from its own clock at receipt (the [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md) bound the STH route already applies"
note: One bound, two reference instants: the STH's published signed_at, and the Registry's clock at receipt. CC 5.3.1 calls its own-clock test the bound "the STH route already applies", so the STH route can be built either way.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "A further peer that offers shaping is admitted by displacement or refused, never run below its class."
side_b: CC 5.4.3: "On any other node the link is made and runs unshaped, a ninth and a tenth connection as the node needs them."
note: The bound paragraph alone reads as refuse the peer; the displacement paragraph makes the link and runs it unshaped on a node that is not shaped-only. Read together they agree (refused a shaped slot); the bound sentence omits the third outcome.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "**Relay is offered by default on every owned node**, the shaped mesh standing on it."
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default, whether or not anyone on it uses the tier."
note: Owned, announced, and (item 4) owner-bound under a root of the genesis charter set are three different sets of nodes that relay by default. An owned node whose binding stays at self relays under the first sentence and not under the other two.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "By default a phone offers relay while it is charging on an unmetered network and reports no capacity otherwise"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "a phone-class node relays by default only on Wi-Fi while charging, and not on battery or on a metered connection"
note: Unmetered network against Wi-Fi: a metered Wi-Fi hotspot and an unmetered wired or cellular link fall differently. constants.tsv phone_relay_default takes "unmetered".

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "One seat holds each mailbox, hour-scale ciphertext only."
side_b: data constants.tsv: 7,200 s (two hours) of ciphertext, read from item 6's delivery statement; the text states only 'hour-scale'
note: The text gives no number for mailbox retention (the route is hourly, the room fallback says two hours); the constant fixes 7,200 s and says itself that the text does not. The first-contact forwarder mailbox borrows the same unstated bound.

side_a: CC 4.1.1: "Consumer policy SHOULD cap the trust weight any single terminal delegate can accumulate from a given root attester at **0.5 × root_trust** by default"
side_b: CC 6.1.8: "the CC 4.1.1 **aggregate-weight cap** (default 0.5 × root_trust) MUST bound the standing one root confers transitively"
note: SHOULD at the home, MUST in the restatement that cites it. C135 reads them as two cases (general policy, and the one bootstrap mechanism); the restatement still names the home's cap as its own.

side_a: CC 6.1.8: "trust-graph **cycles MUST be rejected** (CC 4.1.1)"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "Cycles are visited once, and the cap holds whatever a licensor carries."
note: Reject against visit once. C246 reads them as two graphs (capability delegations, acceptance edges); CC 6.1.8 says "trust-graph", the word CC 4.4.3.8 uses for the acceptance graph.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.12: "Consumer trusts an attestation if `attesting_key_id` has been vouched for by the pinned trust set."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "At each hop the remaining depth is the lesser of what is left and the edge's own."
note: Policy B "adds one hop" over Policy A, yet Policy A already walks to the depth each entry carries (0 to 5). How B's one hop relates to an entry's depth is unstated.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.5 the contract; forward the octets as received)
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 [CC 2.6.1.1](#2.6.1.1) requires it to re-canonicalize member order while holding member presence/absence fixed.
note: CC 2.6.1.1 requires JCS only of a relay "that re-serializes from a parsed object at all"; CC 2.6.1.3 reads it as a duty on every relay that re-emits, and concludes the received octets are the canonical ones. A relay forwarding a pretty-printed envelope verbatim follows 2.6.1.1, 2.6.1.4 and 2.6.1.5 and breaks the premise of 2.6.1.3. Signatures verify either way.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`.
side_b: CC 3.3.2 Both rows above are the frozen snake_case forms.
note: The closed set has two rows (v1 and v2) and decode is "reject an unknown string", so v1 is a known string; the key-grant paragraph, CC 5.1 ("never `v1`") and CC 4.4.3.4.1 make v1 a refusal on every wrap this document describes. The table's v2 row scopes the mandate to "streaming epoch-DEK grants" only, narrower than CC 5.1 ("A DEK that is wrapped MUST be wrapped with v2").

side_a: CC 3.1.2 Carries no version segment (`_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt`): the suffix is the hash.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 a tail on one is tolerated, never required
note: The row says the family carries none; CC 3.1.7 and the manifest note admit a tail, and the match vectors admit identity:canonical_binding:<hash>:v1. A matcher built from the row refuses the tailed form.
